title: Applying Mycelium-Based Materials in Real-World Contexts: The MUSE - MyceliUm SEat Framework
summary: Abstract This paper presents the MUSE - MyceliUm SEat framework as a research-through-design approach for applying mycelium-based materials in real-world contexts. Addressing the gap between experimental biomaterial research and functional
content: Abstract This paper presents the MUSE - MyceliUm SEat framework as a research-through-design approach for applying mycelium-based materials in real-world contexts. Addressing the gap between experimental biomaterial research and functional deployment, the project establishes a cross-scale methodology that moves from extreme performance testing to interior spatial integration. Phase I situates mycelium composites within a high-performance racing environment to accelerate material optimisation under strict structural and ergonomic constraints. Insights from systematic material testing are consolidated into a material matrix adaptable to diverse functional requirements. Phase II translates this knowledge into furniture-scale applications, employing varied fabrication strategies and reciprocal material-form development. The “Living” Room installation functions as a long-term public testbed, enabling evaluation of performance, perception, and ageing under real use conditions. The framework demonstrates how extreme scenarios, interdisciplinary collaboration, and spatial deployment can advance living materials beyond demonstrators toward scalable biodesign practice.

title: Evolving circular pedagogy: a framework for immersive transdisciplinary learning
summary: The contemporary world is undergoing profound socio-economic and environmental transformations that necessitate a radical re-evaluation of how we learn, teach, innovate and engage with research. Traditional educational models are increasing
content: The contemporary world is undergoing profound socio-economic and environmental transformations that necessitate a radical re-evaluation of how we learn, teach, innovate and engage with research. Traditional educational models are increasingly insufficient to address the complexity of the twin transition (i.e. green and digital), in which countries need to identify the most effective strategies to advance the digital and green transformations necessary to support sustainable development. Educational systems and frameworks also need to respond to the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and its three pillars: environment, society, and economy. This research study offers critical insights into the need to build an actionable framework that supports the development of innovative learning spaces and pedagogies within an Immersive Transdisciplinary Learning framework better attuned to the realities of contemporary society. We propose an innovative approach that integrates immersive technologies, transdisciplinary collaboration, and real-world applications to reshape knowledge exchange processes as the learning loop continues to evolve through the lens of Circular Pedagogy.

title: Sustainability as a Lever of Corporate Governance: Challenges, Opportunities and the Role of Universities in Developing Transformative Leaders
summary: Sustainability is a defining feature of contemporary corporate governance, reshaping how organisations conceptualise value creation, accountability, and long-term performance. In South Africa, this transformation is anchored in the King Rep
content: Sustainability is a defining feature of contemporary corporate governance, reshaping how organisations conceptualise value creation, accountability, and long-term performance. In South Africa, this transformation is anchored in the King Reports on Corporate Governance, culminating in King V (2025), which elevates sustainability from implicit integration to an explicit, central governance principle. This chapter develops a theoretically grounded conceptual analysis of sustainability as a lever of corporate governance. Employing a qualitative, interpretive methodology comprising a structured literature review, thematic analysis, abductive theory synthesis, and comparative framework analysis, it maps the convergence of King V, ESG frameworks, and the UN SDGs across 11 governance dimensions and synthesises stakeholder, legitimacy, stewardship, and institutional theories into an integrated explanatory perspective. Illustrative examples from Unilever, Patagonia, and M-PESA/Safaricom ground the argument in documented organisational practice, while persistent implementation gaps, including greenwashing, symbolic compliance, and decoupling, are examined as structural vulnerabilities in sustainability governance. This chapter argues that governance effectiveness ultimately depends on leadership capability, positioning universities as upstream enablers that develop sustainability-capable leaders through the formal curriculum, graduate attributes, and the hidden curriculum. It proposes an original conceptual framework that presents universities as incubators of responsible leadership and sustainability governance. Six conceptual propositions (P1–P6) are advanced, with an agenda for empirical validation. This chapter concludes that sustainability is not an operational adjunct to governance but a transformative force that reconfigures its purpose, processes, and outcomes. Universities have a key role in developing a leadership cadre capable of serving as sustainability-driven change agents.

title: Salivary Biomarkers in the Diagnosis of Periodontal Diseases: From Screening to Personalized Therapy
summary: Periodontal diseases comprise a heterogeneous group of biofilm-associated inflammatory conditions ranging from reversible plaque-induced gingivitis to progressive periodontitis with destruction of the periodontal ligament, cementum, and alv
content: Periodontal diseases comprise a heterogeneous group of biofilm-associated inflammatory conditions ranging from reversible plaque-induced gingivitis to progressive periodontitis with destruction of the periodontal ligament, cementum, and alveolar bone. Conventional diagnosis relies on clinical and radiographic measures that primarily document accumulated tissue damage rather than ongoing molecular activity. Saliva has emerged as an attractive diagnostic medium because it can be collected repeatedly, non-invasively, and at relatively low cost while containing microbial products, inflammatory mediators, tissue-degradation enzymes, bone-remodelling molecules, nucleic acids, metabolites, and proteins derived from periodontal tissues and gingival crevicular fluid. Research has identified matrix metalloproteinase-8, interleukin-1β, interleukin-6, tumour necrosis factor-α, macrophage inflammatory protein-1α, calprotectin, receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand, osteoprotegerin, haemoglobin, selected periodontal pathogens, and multi-omics signatures as promising candidate biomarkers. However, diagnostic performance varies substantially among studies because of differences in periodontal case definitions, saliva collection protocols, analytical platforms, disease severity, systemic comorbidities, smoking exposure, age, medication use, and statistical modelling. This narrative review examines the biological basis, analytical characteristics, and clinical applications of salivary biomarkers in periodontal diseases. Particular attention is given to their potential roles in population screening, differentiation of periodontal health, gingivitis, and periodontitis, identification of active tissue destruction, assessment of progression risk, monitoring of treatment response, and selection of personalized preventive or therapeutic strategies. Evidence supporting single biomarkers is compared with that for composite host–microbial panels, proteomic, metabolomic, transcriptomic, and microbiome-based approaches. Current findings indicate that salivary testing is most appropriately considered an adjunct to, rather than a replacement for, comprehensive periodontal examination. Translation into routine care will require standardized pre-analytical procedures, externally validated thresholds, prospective studies with clinically relevant outcomes, assessment in medically diverse populations, and development of affordable point-of-care technologies. Properly validated salivary biomarker panels could ultimately shift periodontal care from retrospective documentation of tissue loss toward biologically informed screening, risk stratification, and longitudinal disease management. https://doi.org/10.52783/jchr.v16.i4.15783

title: Effect of Different Activation Methods in Production of Activated Charcoal from Palmyrah (Borassus flabellifer L.) Seed Shell and The Formulation of Handwash
source: Journal of Agricultural Sciences – Sri Lanka
summary: Purpose: The objective of the study was to produce and investigate the characteristics of various types of activated charcoal derived from palmyrah (Borassus flabellifer L.) seedshell for the formulation of handwash.Research Method: The dri
content: Purpose: The objective of the study was to produce and investigate the characteristics of various types of activated charcoal derived from palmyrah (Borassus flabellifer L.) seedshell for the formulation of handwash.Research Method: The dried palmyrah seed shells were carbonized and activated chemically and physically at 6000C and 8000C for 45 minutes. Physiochemical and proximate analysis was conducted with commercial activated charcoal to select the best activated charcoal for the formulation of handwash and physiochemical analysis were conducted with commercial handwash.Findings and Values: The chemical activation provided higher yield than physical activation. Different treatments and activation temperature had a significant influence on parameters except moisture content. Surface chemistry analysis demonstrated the existence of hydroxyl, carbonyl, carboxyl, alkyne and aromatic groups similar to commercial activated charcoal. KOH 8000C was selected as best that provides similar result to commercial activated charcoal and used for handwash. Formulated handwash showed similar physiochemical and antimicrobial activity of commercial handwash except pH. Formula 1 with 0.5 % activated charcoal, was selected as the best formulation due to aesthetic attraction. This study provides information and comparison with commercial activated charcoal on physiochemical, proximate and characterization of palmyrah activated charcoal for the industrial application.

title: Biodesigning in a Different Patch: Place, Scale and Regenerative Materialities
summary: Abstract From unceded Australian Country and neighbouring regions, this paper investigates biodesign as a situated, multi-scalar practice, attentive to place, material ecologies, and more‑than‑human relations, reporting from a different ‘pa
content: Abstract From unceded Australian Country and neighbouring regions, this paper investigates biodesign as a situated, multi-scalar practice, attentive to place, material ecologies, and more‑than‑human relations, reporting from a different ‘patch’ to the dominant centre. Drawing on deep‑time Indigenous knowledge systems and emerging biotechnological practices, it contributes a relational, place‑responsive orientation for biodesign, extending its conceptual, ethical, and methodological possibilities. Through auto-ethnographic reflection and case studies spanning Indigenous-led practices, biomaterials research, and regenerative infrastructures, it reveals how biodesign is enacted differently when grounded in specific bioregional, cultural, and material conditions. The practices discussed in the paper demonstrate a bioinclusive aesthetic – embracing growth, decay, contamination, and microbial co‑habitation as regenerative design forces for shaping multispecies futures. Reframing biodesign in this way, as a pluriversal and multi-scalar activity, this study puts forward a set of principles for multi-scalar biodesign that foreground locality, relationality and responsibility when designing with living systems.

title: Tamarind Value Chains for Small-Scale Producers: A Review of Opportunities, Challenges, and Development Pathways
summary: Abstract Tamarind ( Tamarindus indica ) is a multipurpose tree that thrives in arid and semi-arid regions worldwide and supports rural livelihoods through its ecological, economic, and cultural importance. Beyond contributing to household s
content: Abstract Tamarind ( Tamarindus indica ) is a multipurpose tree that thrives in arid and semi-arid regions worldwide and supports rural livelihoods through its ecological, economic, and cultural importance. Beyond contributing to household subsistence and income generation, tamarind products are used in traditional medicine and culinary practices, and sold in local markets. However, its market potential for small-scale producers remains underexplored. This review synthesizes evidence from 32 empirical studies, limited to those published in English between 2000 and 2024, to examine how Indigenous, traditional, and local knowledge, together with value chain dynamics, shape market opportunities for producers. The findings describe how traditional knowledge underpins the widespread use, management, and conservation of tamarind. Nevertheless, market integration is constrained by low species regeneration rates, limited processing and value-addition capacity, weak market linkages, and producers’ limited access to the end market relative to downstream intermediaries. The reviewed studies suggest that realizing tamarind’s potential as a sustainable income-generating product requires interventions that build on Indigenous, traditional, and local knowledge while improving silvicultural practices, strengthening value addition, and expanding equitable market access. Coordinated efforts among policymakers, researchers, extension services, and producers are essential to ensure that increased market participation translates into sustainable socioeconomic benefits for rural communities while supporting long-term resource management.

title: A global comparison of net-zero carbon building practices
summary: Despite extensive research on individual net-zero carbon building (NZCB) practices, prior studies fail to systematically map global adoption patterns across diverse regulatory and market contexts. This study addresses this gap by investigat
content: Despite extensive research on individual net-zero carbon building (NZCB) practices, prior studies fail to systematically map global adoption patterns across diverse regulatory and market contexts. This study addresses this gap by investigating current NZCB practices worldwide. A comprehensive list of global NZCB practices, with associated enablers and barriers, was first identified through a literature review. A global survey was then employed to explore the practical adoption of the practices. Six countries/ regions participated in the survey: Australia, New Zealand, Italy, South Africa, Sri Lanka and Hong Kong. Survey data were analysed using descriptive and frequency analysis. The study identifies three empirically derived adoption patterns: common, varied, and low across countries/regions. Use of solar photovoltaics, energy-efficient HVAC and modular systems were found to be commonly adopted, while advanced technologies like carbon-infused materials were least adopted. Lack of direct financial incentives emerged as the key global barrier, while robust government policies were the main enabler for NZCB adoption worldwide. These findings provide empirical benchmarks for cross-country NZCB adoption and actionable strategies to accelerate low-adoption practices globally.

title: Public versus stakeholder engagement: A distinction for policy-makers to avoid undue interference
source: South African Journal on Human Rights
summary: This paper examines the role of public participation in policy-making, with a focus on public health interventions in South Africa. Public participation processes are crucial for ensuring policies reflect the public good and incorporate the
content: This paper examines the role of public participation in policy-making, with a focus on public health interventions in South Africa. Public participation processes are crucial for ensuring policies reflect the public good and incorporate the lived experiences of diverse communities to develop effective and responsive solutions. However, improper implementation can alienate segments of the population, erode trust and undermine the legitimacy of policy decisions. This paper highlights the concern that participatory processes are often skewed towards powerful stakeholders, such as corporate entities, rather than vulnerable groups who are most in need of public health policies. After delving into the nature of public participation in policy-making processes in South Africa, where and how these processes fall short, as well as how these processes are abused, this paper concludes with suggestions on how participation can be strengthened to reflect the public good.

title: Propositions for facilitating the new Soil Monitoring Law to use private high spatial resolution soil data in EU
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This policy brief provides propositions for facilitating the new Soil Monitoring Law to use private high spatial resolution soil data in EU. This policy brief was funded by the European Union's Horizon Europe research and innovation program
content: This policy brief provides propositions for facilitating the new Soil Monitoring Law to use private high spatial resolution soil data in EU. This policy brief was funded by the European Union's Horizon Europe research and innovation programme, Grant Agreement No. 101112951 (Driving high-level conversations to shape carbon farming markets and policies - CREDIBLE; https://www.project-credible.eu/).

title: Understanding and suppressing gas evolution in lithium metal batteries with ether-based electrolytes
summary: Understanding and suppressing gas evolution is critical to enabling high-energy-density lithium metal batteries (LMBs). Yet, comprehensive investigations in ether-based systems remain limited. Here we quantify gas generation in ether-based
content: Understanding and suppressing gas evolution is critical to enabling high-energy-density lithium metal batteries (LMBs). Yet, comprehensive investigations in ether-based systems remain limited. Here we quantify gas generation in ether-based LMBs and elucidate the underlying mechanisms. We link CO and CO2 production to the cathode, and CH4 evolution to the anode. Notably, CO and CO2 are consumed at the Li anode to form Li-containing species such as Li2CO3. Although CH4 ultimately dominates the gaseous products, its evolution during cycling is delayed until a distinct onset point. We show that in a high-concentration ether electrolyte, anode activation improves Li deposition morphology and suppresses interfacial reactions, extending the number of cycles to gas onset and cell failure by an order of magnitude. Achieving these gains without altering the electrolyte enables the reconsideration of seemingly impractical electrolytes, highlighting a practical strategy to enhance the safety and performance of commercial LMBs. Gas evolution compromises the safety and commercial viability of high-energy lithium metal batteries. Now it has been shown that CH4 generated by ether-based electrolyte decomposition at the Li anode dominates gas evolution. A facile anode activation strategy suppresses CH4-forming interfacial reactions, dramatically reducing gas evolution and extending cycle life.

title: Coordination regimes, treaty layering and governance congestion in global biodiversity governance: The International Big Cat Alliance
summary: Global biodiversity governance has expanded into a dense regime complex of overlapping institutions, generating risks of fragmentation and coordination challenges. In response, governance arrangements increasingly emphasise coordination acr
content: Global biodiversity governance has expanded into a dense regime complex of overlapping institutions, generating risks of fragmentation and coordination challenges. In response, governance arrangements increasingly emphasise coordination across existing frameworks, yet their systemic implications remain under-examined. This paper develops the concept of coordination-oriented meta-regimes as an analytical lens to examine how treaty-based arrangements may reshape regime complexity. Using the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) as an exploratory case, this paper analyses its institutional architecture. The findings suggest that IBCA introduces additional organisational structures, reporting systems and financial channels within an already dense biodiversity governance landscape. This highlights how treaty-based coordination arrangements may contribute to institutional congestion and governance sclerosis through cumulative layering. Under certain conditions, these dynamics may generate governance congestion and institutional sclerosis, with fragmentation risks emerging as a secondary consequence.

title: Identifying strategies to improve the water productivity of permanent raised beds
source: University of Southern Queensland ePrints (University of Southern Queensland)
summary: Permanent raised bed (PRB) farming systems combine several elements (e.g. reduced tillage, controlled traffic, stubble retention) of conservation agriculture. PRB systems have recently been introduced into irrigated areas but there is a lac
content: Permanent raised bed (PRB) farming systems combine several elements (e.g. reduced tillage, controlled traffic, stubble retention) of conservation agriculture. PRB systems have recently been introduced into irrigated areas but there is a lack of information on the agronomic and irrigation performance of these systems under these conditions. Three years of field research into the performance of irrigated PRBs was conducted in south east Queensland, Australia and north west Pakistan. These studies benchmarked the irrigation performance of variously sized PRB systems and explored the impact of bed renovation method (no tillage (NT), shallow cultivation (SC) and blade ploughing (BP)) on soil hydro-physical properties (bulk density, soil moisture storage, infiltration), irrigation performance, crop yield and input water productivity (WP). Irrigation management strategies to improve lateral infiltration and irrigation performance were also investigated. The initial benchmarking study was conducted on two farms with clayey Vertisol (Australia) and three farms with sandy clay loam, Alfisol, (Pakistan) soils. The results showed low irrigation performance with excessive deep drainage potential. The irrigation application efficiency (Ea) on the clayey Vertisol and sandy clay loam was as low as 68% and 50%, requirement efficiency (Er) 96% and 77% and distribution uniformity (DU) 86% and 66%, respectively. However, the majority of the narrow beds (66 cm furrow spacing) were over-irrigated on the sandy clay loam while the wide beds (132 cm furrow spacing) were under-irrigated. Inappropriate renovation and bed furrow dimensions, sub-optimal irrigation management and poor lateral infiltration were the main factors likely to affect WP of irrigated PRBs. The evaluation of bed renovation methods found that BP on the clayey Vertisol reduced (~6%) the average seasonal bulk density of the surface 0-30 cm compared to the NT treatment. BP was found to produce higher lateral infiltration into the beds than either NT or SC. Freshly applied BP and SC produced a higher (~23%) cumulative infiltration than NT but the effect was transient and was not significant in the following season when the PRB renovation treatments were not freshly applied. The SC beds slump more than the BP and NT beds. The soil water content in the beds indicated that there was increased water storage associated with BP. PRB renovation (i.e. SC or BP) was found to reduce irrigation performance on the clayey Vertisol when the irrigation was farmer managed. The volume of irrigation water applied to the fresh SC and BP treatments increased by up 13% and 55%, and Ea was reduced by up to 9% and 29% respectively, compared with NT during the 2010 wheat and 2011 corn seasons. NT produced a higher wheat yield and WP, but the lower wheat yield in the cultivated treatments was associated with poor crop establishment from a rough soil surface and inadequate seeder performance in this season. title: DISPOSIÇÃO FINAL DE RESÍDUOS SÓLIDOS E EMISSÕES DE GEE: A INFLUÊNCIA DO BRASIL NA CRISE CLIMÁTICA GLOBAL
summary: O estudo analisa a relação entre a disposição final de resíduos sólidos urbanos e as emissões de gases de efeito estufa do setor de Resíduos no Brasil, discutindo o papel do país na crise climática global. Trata-se de uma pesquisa aplicada,
content: O estudo analisa a relação entre a disposição final de resíduos sólidos urbanos e as emissões de gases de efeito estufa do setor de Resíduos no Brasil, discutindo o papel do país na crise climática global. Trata-se de uma pesquisa aplicada, de abordagem quantitativa e caráter descritivo, fundamentada em dados secundários do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística, do Sistema de Estimativas de Emissões e Remoções de Gases de Efeito Estufa e da Associação Brasileira de Resíduos e Meio Ambiente, complementados por revisão de literatura científica. O objetivo foi avaliar a evolução histórica das emissões do setor, sua distribuição entre os estados brasileiros e sua projeção para os próximos 20 anos, a partir do Censo Demográfico de 2022. Os resultados mostram que a disposição final em aterros sanitários e lixões responde por cerca de dois terços das emissões do setor, com ritmo de crescimento superior ao das demais fontes, e que a distribuição espacial das emissões acompanha a concentração populacional e econômica do país. A projeção construída a partir do crescimento populacional estimado até 2042 indica pressão adicional sobre as emissões do setor, exceto em cenários que incorporem metas de aproveitamento energético do biogás gerado em aterros sanitários. Conclui-se que a mitigação das emissões do setor de resíduos no Brasil depende da combinação entre redução na fonte, ampliação da reciclagem e efetiva captação do biogás gerado na disposição final.

title: How Do ESG and Innovation Strategies Affect Bank Performance and Risk Stability? Panel Evidence from Taiwan’s Banking Industry
summary: Sustainable finance, digital financial innovation, and green innovation have become central strategic pressures in banking, yet their joint effects on bank performance and risk remain insufficiently understood. This study develops an integr
content: Sustainable finance, digital financial innovation, and green innovation have become central strategic pressures in banking, yet their joint effects on bank performance and risk remain insufficiently understood. This study develops an integrated ESG-innovation framework and examines quarterly panel data for 24 Taiwanese financial holding and domestic commercial banks from 2016Q1 to 2025Q3, yielding 934 bank-quarter observations. Return on assets (ROA) and the Z-score are used to capture operating performance and financial stability, respectively, and bank fixed-effects panel models are estimated for high- and low-ESG as well as high- and low-innovation subsamples. The re-estimated results reveal a conditional sustainability effect: ESG and innovation do not generate homogeneous financial benefits, but depend on banks’ ESG foundations, innovation intensity, leverage, and scale. Environmental scores are positively associated with ROA in the high-ESG subsample and weakly positive in the low-ESG subsample, whereas credit card transaction expansion is costly for low-ESG banks. In high-innovation banks, credit card transaction volume and green patents are negatively associated with ROA, suggesting adjustment costs and diminishing marginal returns. For financial stability, ESG recognition and green patents are more beneficial in lower ESG or innovation contexts, while leverage is consistently negative across all specifications. These findings contribute to the sustainable finance literature by clarifying how ESG, FinTech-related innovation, and green innovation jointly shape bank performance and risk in a policy-driven emerging market. The results also suggest that banks and regulators should adopt differentiated ESG and innovation strategies rather than assuming that sustainability investment produces uniform outcomes.

title: Addressing agricultural challenges in Tanzania using a systematic review approach to youth employment transformation
summary: Tanzania’s agricultural sector is vital to the national economy and rural livelihoods but faces significant challenges, which in most cases, hinder productivity and youth employment. The sector has strong potential for youth employment, as
content: Tanzania’s agricultural sector is vital to the national economy and rural livelihoods but faces significant challenges, which in most cases, hinder productivity and youth employment. The sector has strong potential for youth employment, as it provides opportunities across multiple generations. However, high youth unemployment is likely to be linked to the sector’s limited transformation and structural challenges within the broader economy. On that basis, it was imperative to systematically assess and itemize the specific challenges hindering the sector’s contribution to employment and devise a plan and strategies to address those challenges. Using a Boolean search, a systematic review of 69 articles, published between the year 2005 and 2025, from the Web of Science and Scopus was conducted using the keywords (“Tanzania” OR “United Republic of Tanzania”) AND (agricultur* OR agribusiness OR “agricultural value chain”) AND (youth OR “young people”) AND (employ OR livelihood OR “create job”) AND (challeng* OR barriers OR constraints OR transform). The search was limited to the title, abstract, and keywords, and the review involved: records identified through database searching (520); records after duplicates were removed (360); records screened (360); records excluded (200); full-text articles assessed for eligibility (160); full-text articles excluded with reasons (91); and finally, 69 articles were selected for the review. The findings exhibit that agriculture presents substantial opportunities for youth employment across the value chain from production to processing, marketing, and digital services. However, youth participation remains constrained by limited access to land, finance, skills, agricultural extension services, climate change impacts, and markets. Similarly, the structural transformation remains slow due to limited manufacturing growth and insufficient agro-processing development. Fortunately, the review also identified some opportunities which can be harnessed for the development of the sector. Some of these include; agricultural innovation, agribusiness development, and inclusive policy frameworks. The study synthesizes insights from research and development programs to propose a framework that focuses on multi-stakeholder collaboration, climate-resilient practices, and youth-centered interventions. These findings inform strategies for addressing agricultural constraints and promoting sustainable youth employment, contributing to broader socio-economic resilience and inclusive growth in Tanzania.

title: Phytofabricated Metal Oxide Nanoparticles as Nano-Biostimulants for Salinity Stress Mitigation: Mechanisms, Agronomic Applications, and Translational Challenges
source: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
summary: Soil salinization is one of the most widely distributed abiotic factors limiting global crop production. It encompasses over 833 million hectares of land in the world and is a major factor in food insecurity in arid, semi-arid and irrigated
content: Soil salinization is one of the most widely distributed abiotic factors limiting global crop production. It encompasses over 833 million hectares of land in the world and is a major factor in food insecurity in arid, semi-arid and irrigated areas. Traditional salinity management practices-leaching, gypsum amendment, developing tolerant cultivars and chemical priming-are still only partial, slow and costly measures. In the past decade, phytofabricated (plant-mediated, "green") metal-oxide nanoparticles (MO-NPs) with the small-size reactivity of engineered nanomaterials (ENMs) and biocompatibility of the phytochemical capping agents have been developed as a new generation of nano-biostimulants. This review critically synthesizes knowledge on the effects of phytofabricated MO-NPs on reducing salinity stress in agronomically important crops. The chemistry of plant-extract mediated synthesis, advantages over the chemical and physical methods, and role of plant secondary metabolites (polyphenols, flavonoids, terpenoids and alkaloids) in particle stabilization and bioactivity is discussed. The mechanistic core includes six interconnected axes: (i) scavenging and modulation of reactive oxygen-species (ROS), (ii) restoration of Na?/K? homeostasis through regulation of the SOS, NHX and HKT transporters, (iii) accumulation of osmoprotectants (proline, glycine betaine and soluble sugars), (iv) protection of the photosynthetic apparatus and membrane stability, (v) hormonal and nitric-oxide signalling, and (vi) nano-specific properties (nanozyme activity). We assess agronomic performance of wheat, maize, rice, soybean, tomato, barley and legumes-synergies with biochar, PGPR and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi. Last, the concept of translational bottlenecks (dose-dependent phytotoxicity and soil-microbiome perturbation, environmental persistence, regulatory ambiguity, and scalability of phytofabrication) is introduced, and a forward agenda is proposed, focusing on multi-omics integration, field validation, smart delivery, and AI-guided synthesis. However, the use of Phytofabricated MO-NPs in salinity management has enormous potential but needs to be backed by evidence-based deployment of crop-specific and ecologically informed use.

title: The Call of Wilderness: A Historical Analysis of Western Hiking Development and Its Implications for China's Outdoor Recreation Transition
source: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
summary: In recent years, as the rapid development of the Internet, outdoor activities have become a popular trend among Chinese people. However, this sudden spread of outdoor activities is accompanied by gear-centered consumption and huge environme
content: In recent years, as the rapid development of the Internet, outdoor activities have become a popular trend among Chinese people. However, this sudden spread of outdoor activities is accompanied by gear-centered consumption and huge environmental cost. Therefore, this study aims to analyze the underlying mechanisms behind these two issues, exploring possible resolutions in different angles. In doing so, this study analyzed second-hand materials to compare the developmental history in both the West and China, determining to gain insights from Western experiences. Eventually, this study discovered that the gear-centered consumption originated from people's demand, fashioned by the Internet, for social identity and misleading online contents. It also found that the environmental cost is the result of a lack of education and regulation. Therefore, to solve these problems, multiple approaches should be implemented simultaneously. It is essential to build an authoritative platform of outdoor information, to promote affordability and sustainability in the market of outdoor equipment, to improve environmental education, and to strengthen regulation on people who attend outdoor activities.

title: Three Decades of Silviculture in Northern Rocky Mountain Forests, USA: Trends, Practices, and Outcomes
summary: Abstract The Northern Rocky Mountains region includes 42 million acres of forest land which is diverse in landownership, management objectives, tree species, site productivities, disturbance regimes, and silvicultural practices resulting in
content: Abstract The Northern Rocky Mountains region includes 42 million acres of forest land which is diverse in landownership, management objectives, tree species, site productivities, disturbance regimes, and silvicultural practices resulting in a mosaic landscape. Substantial changes in landownership, management objectives, markets, policy, forest conditions, and silvicultural practices have occurred over the last thirty years. This review provides a synopsis of these changes across different forest types in the region. The U.S. Department of Agriculture, Forest Service remains the largest forest management entity in the region, encompassing all forest types. Silvicultural practices have largely shifted towards multiple objective management on federal lands, reflecting broad societal values. This includes restoring historical species composition and enhancing resistance and resilience to natural disturbances, with wildfire a dominant disturbance concern across all forest types. Large corporate landownerships remain concentrated on high productivity sites in the region. Many of these companies are now Timber Investment Management Organizations (TIMOs) and Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs). The region has seen an uptick in the establishment of high-yield plantations on their land, dominated by Douglas-fir and western larch. State lands continue to manage to meet their endowment mandates with some examples of increased intensification through plantation establishment. Overall, the region is dynamic, and we expect continued emphasis on fuels reduction, timber production, recreation, wildlife habitat, among others, as meeting these objectives will help ensure the sustainability of forests for years to come.

title: The Miocene extensional Pannonian Superbasin, volume 2: Geoenergy exploration: introduction
summary: This volume, dealing with the geoenergy aspects of the Pannonian Basin, builds on the previous one which described the regional geology of this basin. For the petroleum industry the Pannonian Basin is a actually a “Superbasin” as it reached
content: This volume, dealing with the geoenergy aspects of the Pannonian Basin, builds on the previous one which described the regional geology of this basin. For the petroleum industry the Pannonian Basin is a actually a “Superbasin” as it reached approximately 13 billion barrels of oil (equivalent) cumulative production to date. As to the yet-to-find hydrocarbon resources in this very mature basin complex, another >5 billion barrels may be found based on various estimates. The Pannonian Basin, like most Superbasins, has several source rocks, stacked reservoirs, a greater than 6-km-thick basin fill, large amounts of subsurface data, multiple operators, mature infrastructure and direct access to markets. The ongoing energy transition requires a new look at this large European basin complex. In this volume not only hydrocarbon-related but many other geoenergy aspects are addressed. Various chapters are dedicated to geothermal energy, carbon storage and sequestration, hydrogen and natural gas storage, and critical mineral exploration (including lithium, helium and natural hydrogen). In particular, the Pannonian Basin is the hottest sedimentary basin in mainland Europe, with a long history of geothermal energy usage and research. Therefore, it also provides a useful template for geothermal exploration and utilization projects in other extensional basins worldwide.

title: Facilitation or Loafing: the intensity and type of tourist-host interaction’s influence on tourists’ pro-environmental behavior intention
summary: From the perspective of tourist-host interaction, the study explores the dual impact of the relationship between interaction intensity and interaction type (social-oriented interaction, service-oriented interaction) on tourists’ pro-environ
content: From the perspective of tourist-host interaction, the study explores the dual impact of the relationship between interaction intensity and interaction type (social-oriented interaction, service-oriented interaction) on tourists’ pro-environmental behavior intention (PEBI). The results show that in the social-oriented interaction, a higher level of interaction can effectively stimulate tourists’ emotional solidarity, thus enhancing their PEBI. In service-oriented interaction, the higher the interaction intensity, the more psychological entitlement the tourists would be stimulated to have, which would in turn reduce their willingness to engage in PEBI. By comprehensively exploring the mechanisms by which interaction affects tourists’ PEBI, this study constructs a theoretical model of the effects of interaction type and interaction intensity on tourists’ PEBI, which provides targeted environmental management strategies for destination managers to help guide tourists to actively protect the environment, thereby promoting the sustainable development of scenic spots.

title: Balanced Risk Assessment and Management in Development of Hard-To-Recover Reserves Using Example of Heavy Oil
summary: Depletion of conventional oil fields and increasing requirements for the economic justification of investment projects enhance the significance of developing hard-to-recover reserves, including heavy oil, which is characterized by technolog
content: Depletion of conventional oil fields and increasing requirements for the economic justification of investment projects enhance the significance of developing hard-to-recover reserves, including heavy oil, which is characterized by technological complexity, high energy intensity, and multifactor uncertainty. This study proposes a balanced risk assessment framework that integrates Monte Carlo simulation with a Mamdani-type fuzzy inference system. Quantitative project parameters are modeled as random variables, while poorly formalized geological, technical, operational, environmental, social, and political-regulatory risks are aggregated into an integral fuzzy risk index. The proposed framework is tested using open data for a heavy oil project and four integration variants: a baseline Monte Carlo model without fuzzy risk adjustment, a model with risk-adjusted mean values, a model with risk-adjusted standard deviations, and a combined model. The fuzzy inference system produced a high integral risk index, Rhtr = 0.782. In the baseline model, expected NPV was −1.79 billion USD and the probability of negative NPV was 66.52%. When the integral risk index was incorporated through shifts in expected values, expected NPV decreased to approximately −6.76 billion USD and the probability of negative NPV increased to 89.90%. The combined model produced a similar central shift, with expected NPV of −6.75 billion USD and P(NPV < 0) of 89.44%, while also reflecting increased distributional uncertainty. The results show that the main economic effect of integral risk is associated with systematic changes in expected CAPEX, OPEX, production rate, and decline rate, whereas variance-only adjustment has limited influence on central project metrics. The proposed approach provides a transparent tool for linking qualitative risk assessment with probabilistic economic evaluation and supports more conservative investment decision-making in heavy oil development projects.

title: Evidence on the use of the regional digital transformation concept: systematic literature review
summary: Abstract This systematic literature review examines the use of the emergent concept of regional digital transformation by analysing 62 peer-reviewed research articles that employ this term. The findings provide significant insights, reveali
content: Abstract This systematic literature review examines the use of the emergent concept of regional digital transformation by analysing 62 peer-reviewed research articles that employ this term. The findings provide significant insights, revealing that the concept exists in the literature, is being used with increasing frequency, but as a working concept and not as a theoretical construction, and is applied inconsistently across contexts. The results are organised into four principal themes: (1) the association with geographical areas characterised by specific attributes; (2) the strong linkage to regional innovation; (3) the employment of the term in measurement processes; and (4) the connection to state policies, including digital policies, strategies, or programmes. The review also shows that digital transformation processes within a particular region are highly variable, contingent upon regional context. Furthermore, a bibliometric analysis was conducted to elucidate term correlations and to clarify the evolution of the concept. The results indicate a robust correlation among the terms digital transformation, development, effect, and region in relation to regional digital transformation.

title: The Impact of Sustainable Development Concepts on Urban Structure: A Comparative Analysis of Global Urban Experiences)
source: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science
summary: Background: The urban structure of cities plays a vital role in determining the paths and directions of urban development. With the accelerating pace of contemporary urban sprawl, sustainability has become an urgent necessity to achieve a b
content: Background: The urban structure of cities plays a vital role in determining the paths and directions of urban development. With the accelerating pace of contemporary urban sprawl, sustainability has become an urgent necessity to achieve a balance between economic growth, social justice, and environmental protection. Over the past fifty years, several planning concepts—such as Transit-Oriented Development (TOD), neo-urbanization, and smart growth—have emerged with the aim of reducing reliance on private vehicles and transforming cities into human-centered environments. However, a gap remains in evaluating the urban outcomes of these concepts on a global comparative scale. Objective: This study aims to research and apply the concepts of sustainable urban development and determine their structural, functional, and visual impact on the urban structure and fabric of contemporary cities. Methodology: The study employs dual research methodology. First, it includes a literature review of the theories and approaches related to forms of sustainable cities (compact cities, eco-cities, neo-traditional development, and urban sprawl control). Secondly, it includes a comparative inductive analysis of five leading global urban experiences: Barcelona (Spain), Amsterdam (Netherlands), Curitiba (Brazil), Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia), and Melbourne (Australia), to identify urban threats and the planning policies implemented in each. Results: The results showed that successful sustainable urban transformation is fundamentally based on shifting the design philosophy from car-centric infrastructure to human-centered spaces. The comparative analysis demonstrated that integrating smart and sustainable public transportation systems (such as Bus Rapid Transit and tram networks) with mixed land uses directly contributes to containing unplanned sprawl and increasing green spaces and pedestrian walkways. Conversely, the research revealed significant challenges to this implementation, most notably: the high financial costs associated with establishing and maintaining sustainable infrastructure, the continuous need for data updates, and the extensive reliance on government spending. Conclusion: The study concludes that urban sustainability is determined by the complex interaction of three key elements: land, population, and urban activity. To ensure quality of life, urban administrations must adopt integrated, multidisciplinary planning frameworks that balance natural and built elements, achieving high architectural and environmental standards that support the health and well-being of residents.

title: Peanut Hulls: Their Properties and Potential Uses
source: Bulletin of Miscellaneous Information (Royal Gardens Kew)
summary: Peanut hulls are already used for poultry litter, filler in artificial fireplace logs, and roughage in cattle feed. Potential additional uses, most of which have not been systematically investigated, are pet litter, mushroom-growing medium,
content: Peanut hulls are already used for poultry litter, filler in artificial fireplace logs, and roughage in cattle feed. Potential additional uses, most of which have not been systematically investigated, are pet litter, mushroom-growing medium, carrier for pesticides and fertilizers, mulch, fuel, absorbent for molasses, fillers, drycleaner, absorbent for oil spills, anticaking material, floor-sweeping compound, foundry-sand component, sealant in oil-drilling muds, metal polish, and charcoal briquets and activated carbon. The principal advantages recommending hulls for many uses are high absorbency (a method for determining water absorption is given), chemical inertness, concentrated supply at shelling plants, and low cost. Their principal disadvantage, bulkiness, which results in high transportation costs, seems to limit their potential to the development of markets near the source of supply.

title: AI/ML in Chemical Engineering: From molecular design to industrial process optimization
source: Chemical and Process Engineering New Frontiers
summary: The integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into chemical engineering represents a paradigm transformation that fundamentally reconceptualizes practice across molecular, process, and industrial scales. This comprehensive
content: The integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into chemical engineering represents a paradigm transformation that fundamentally reconceptualizes practice across molecular, process, and industrial scales. This comprehensive narrative review synthesizes recent advances in AI/ML methodologies, including graph neural networks, physics-informed neural networks, deep reinforcement learning, and generative artificial intelligence – and critically evaluates their applications spanning molecular property prediction, catalyst design, pharmaceutical development, reactor optimization, process control, and sustainability initiatives. Contemporary AI/ML approaches demonstrate unprecedented capabilities in navigating complex multiscale phenomena while maintaining computational tractability and physical interpretability. Landmark achievements include 71% reduction in experimental iterations for reaction optimization through deep reinforcement learning, 98% accuracy in predictive maintenance using LSTM-based fault detection, sub-1% prediction errors in virtual metrology for semiconductor manufacturing, and substantial improvements incarbon capture efficiency through machine learning-guided materials discovery. Physics-informed neural networks address the critical challenge of plant-model mismatch by synergistically integrating mechanistic knowledge with data-driven learning, enabling extrapolation beyond training domains while respecting conservation laws. Explainable AI techniques, particularly SHAP analysis, enhance operational acceptance by 52% in safety-critical applications through transparent decision-making pathways. Despite remarkable progress, persistent challenges remain in data quality and standardization, model interpretability for regulatory compliance, computational scalability for real-time control, and integration with legacy industrial infrastructure. The review identifies transformative future directions including multi-modal learning frameworks, transfer learning for data-scarce applications, quantum machine learning for molecular design, and human-AI collaborative systems. Successful deployment demands interdisciplinary collaboration uniting chemical engineering domain expertise with computational intelligence, guided by principles of transparency, reproducibility, and responsible innovation to address sustainability imperatives while maintaining operational excellence and safety in chemical manufacturing.

title: PENGARUH CORPORATE GOVERNANCE DAN KINERJA LINGKUNGAN TERHADAP CARBON EMISSION DISCLOSURE DENGAN SISTEM MANAJEMEN LINGKUNGAN SEBAGAI VARIABEL MODERASI
summary: Penelitian ini memiliki tujuan teruntuk melakukan tindakan analisis terhadap pengaruh Corporate Governance serta Kinerja Lingkungan pada Carbon Emission Disclosure dengan Sistem Manajemen Lingkungan sebagai variabel moderasi. Populasi yang
content: Penelitian ini memiliki tujuan teruntuk melakukan tindakan analisis terhadap pengaruh Corporate Governance serta Kinerja Lingkungan pada Carbon Emission Disclosure dengan Sistem Manajemen Lingkungan sebagai variabel moderasi. Populasi yang ada pada riset ini ialah perusahaan non keuangan yang sudah tercatat di Bursa Efek Indonesia pada rentang tahun 2017–2020 dengan sampel yang berjumlah sebanyak 25 perusahaan. Data yang dipergunakan ialah data sekunder yang diambilnya dari annual report serta juga sustainability report. Teknik analisis yang diterapkan ialah regresi linear berganda. Hasil dari riset memperlihatkan bahwasanya Corporate Governance yang diproksikan melalui board size serya board independence serta kinerja lingkungan berpengaruh negatif pada carbon emission disclosure, sedangkan audit committees dan Sistem Manajemen Lingkungan berpengaruhnya secara positif serta signifikan pada carbon emission disclosure. Selain itu, Sistem Manajemen Lingkungan tidaklah memperkuat pengaruh dari board independence, board size, serta kinerja lingkungan yang ada pada carbon emission disclosure, namun memperkuat pengaruh audit committees pada carbon emission disclosure.

title: China Carbon Emission Trading Market Multivariate Time Series Dataset (2014–2022)
summary: This dataset contains raw multivariate time series data from three pilot carbon markets (Beijing, Hubei and Shenzhen), as well as a unified result dataset with completed missing value imputation. All data are stored in Excel format and can
content: This dataset contains raw multivariate time series data from three pilot carbon markets (Beijing, Hubei and Shenzhen), as well as a unified result dataset with completed missing value imputation. All data are stored in Excel format and can be directly loaded for subsequent analysis and modeling without additional missing value imputation procedures. The accompanying code retains scripts for cross-market correlation and nonlinear causality analysis, as well as the full implementation of the proposed MIMO-BiLSTM-Attention-GARCH integrated forecasting framework. This dataset supports relevant research on multivariate time series joint representation learning, cross-market linkage modeling and carbon price forecasting algorithm validation.

title: Cathode and anode materials for alkali metal electrochemical reactions in energy storage systems – current state of the art and potential developments
source: Chemical and Process Engineering New Frontiers
summary: European and world economies are displaying increased use of renewable energy sources (RES). Energy sources such as wind energy, solar energy and water current energy, while clean and not emitting carbon dioxide, do not allow for stable ele
content: European and world economies are displaying increased use of renewable energy sources (RES). Energy sources such as wind energy, solar energy and water current energy, while clean and not emitting carbon dioxide, do not allow for stable electrical energy production due to their dependence on weather conditions. Current development trends are focused on the production of energy storage units, which will allow for stable electricity production from renewable sources. One unit investigated by researchers is flow and steady state high-capacity batteries. Ideal storage system should be characterised by high electric stability, charge-discharge reversibility, stability and low cost. The most widely used technology is ion lithium batteries. However, sources of lithium are geographically and quantitatively limited. There is an increasing interest in the application of other active metals in energy storage systems. Most active metal salts exhibit high water solubility and are available in most parts of the world. The objective of this work was to catalogue known active metals usage in energy storage, including their current and most promising applications, with a focus on the capacity of electrochemical processes and on anode and cathode materials.

title: The contribution of the surface temperature inversion to Antarctic warming
summary: Abstract. Antarctica is expected to warm faster than the global average throughout the 21st century in a phenomenon called Antarctic amplification. The polar atmosphere is unique in having a strong and persistent surface temperature inversi
content: Abstract. Antarctica is expected to warm faster than the global average throughout the 21st century in a phenomenon called Antarctic amplification. The polar atmosphere is unique in having a strong and persistent surface temperature inversion layer, and its changing properties can dramatically affect polar warming. In this work, we reveal mechanisms behind Antarctic amplification by quantifying the contribution of this surface temperature inversion to the region’s near-surface warming. Global climate models often miss the vertical resolution and physical processes needed to correctly simulate the intense near-surface inversion. Here, we downscale four global climate models with the regional climate model MAR (Modèle Atmosphérique Régional) to decompose the Antarctic near-surface potential temperature into the background potential temperature and the surface temperature inversion strength. From the late 20th to the late 21st century, we attribute 72 % of July near-surface warming over the Antarctic continent and sea ice to large-scale background warming under the Shared Socioeconomic Pathway SSP5-8.5. However, the spatial variability in this warming is driven by surface processes through their weakening of the surface temperature inversion, which explains the remaining 28 % of warming. Over the ocean, this weakening is well predicted by sea ice loss, and accounts for 41 % of the near-surface warming. By contrast, the weakening of the inversion explains 16 % of near-surface warming on the continent, where it is correlated with stronger present-day atmospheric stability, which suggests that the lapse-rate feedback contributes significantly to spatial variability in warming. The particularly strong contribution of sea ice loss to the weakening of the inversion could explain the asymmetry between Arctic and Antarctic amplification. Variability in the inversion strength could also account for discrepancies between paleoclimate proxy records.

title: Stuffed toys as a source of oral PFAS exposure: Migration into artificial saliva and exposure assessment
source: Journal of Exposure Science & Environmental Epidemiology
summary: BACKGROUND: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widely used in textiles and consumer products, resulting in ubiquitous human exposure. Infants and young children may experience distinct exposure patterns due to mouthing behavior,
content: BACKGROUND: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widely used in textiles and consumer products, resulting in ubiquitous human exposure. Infants and young children may experience distinct exposure patterns due to mouthing behavior, yet oral exposure from textile-based products such as stuffed toys remains poorly characterized. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to quantify saliva-mediated PFAS migration from commercially available stuffed toys under mouthing-relevant conditions, assess the potential contribution to early-life exposure, and evaluate the effectiveness of washing as a mitigation measure. METHODS: Eighteen stuffed toys intended for infants and toddlers were analysed. PFAS migration was assessed using artificial saliva under standardized conditions and quantified by Liquid Chromatography-Tandem Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Deterministic exposure assessment was performed to estimate daily and weekly intake, complemented by margin of exposure (MOE) calculations and reverse dosimetry based on biomonitoring data. The effect of a standardized water-rinsing step on PFAS migration was also investigated. RESULTS: PFAS were detected in all toys, with migration profiles dominated by short-chain perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids, particularly perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA). A limited number of toys accounted for most of the PFAS released. Estimated intakes for EFSA-regulated PFAS (perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS), perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), perfluorohexanesulfonic acid (PFHxS), perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA)) remained below the tolerable weekly intake (TWI), whereas MOE and reverse-dosimetry analyses highlighted compound- and product-specific exposure relevance for short-chain and emerging PFAS. Washing reduced PFAS migration in most cases but increased migration for some PFAS and products, indicating heterogeneous and non-systematic effects. IMPACT: This study demonstrates that stuffed toys represent a relevant and often underappreciated source of early-life PFAS exposure. PFAS migration was observed across all products and was dominated by short-chain compounds, with perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA) emerging as the main driver of exposure relevance. While intake of EFSA-regulated PFAS remained below guidance values, PFHxA showed a large influence on exposure metrics, including reduced MOE and high relative contributions in reverse-dosimetry analyses. These findings reveal an important regulatory and knowledge gap for emerging PFAS and highlight the need to integrate mouthing-relevant exposure pathways into risk assessment of products intended for young children.

title: Xi Jinping's Thought on Ecological Civilization: Its Original Contribution to Marxist Ecological Theory and Its Practical Expansion
source: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
summary: Xi Jinping's Thought on Ecological Civilization represents the latest achievement of the Sinicization and modernization of Marxist ecological theory. It systematically addresses the major issues of why ecological civilization should be buil
content: Xi Jinping's Thought on Ecological Civilization represents the latest achievement of the Sinicization and modernization of Marxist ecological theory. It systematically addresses the major issues of why ecological civilization should be built in the new era, what kind of ecological civilization should be built, and how it should be built. This paper takes Marxist basic principles as its foundation and, around the dimensions of natural wealth, people's position, ecological justice, carbon governance, digital governance, Party leadership, and global ecological governance, elucidates its original contributions to the theory of productive forces, the laws of socialist construction, the national governance system, and the global ecological discourse. The study finds that Xi Jinping's Thought on Ecological Civilization takes the harmonious coexistence of man and nature as its value orientation, green new-quality productive forces as its practical support, and institutional advantages and international dissemination as important guarantees, providing scientific guidance for promoting the construction of Beautiful China and building a clean and beautiful world.

title: Women and climate adaptation in South Africa: a gender-responsive policy review
summary: Introduction This article examines how South African climate adaptation policies conceptualize and operationalise gender-responsive adaptation, with particular attention to women's vulnerability, agency, and participation in climate governa
content: Introduction This article examines how South African climate adaptation policies conceptualize and operationalise gender-responsive adaptation, with particular attention to women's vulnerability, agency, and participation in climate governance. Methods Rather than employing a systematic review, the study adopts a qualitative policy review and interpretive analysis, drawing on peer-reviewed academic literature, national legislation and policy documents, government strategies, and international normative frameworks related to gender equality, climate adaptation, and disaster risk reduction. The study conducted a review of 14 purposively chosen policy documents, such as the National Climate Change Adaptation strategy, the Climate Change Act 2024, and the National Development Plan. This review employed thematic coding, drawing on Intersectionality Theory and the Gender and Development (GAD) Approach. Results and Discussion The analysis reveals that while South Africa has developed comprehensive climate and development policies, gender considerations remain weakly operationalised within adaptation planning and implementation. Structural barriers, including inadequate gender mainstreaming, limited gender-responsive budgeting, fragmented institutional coordination, and insufficient political commitment, continue to constrain women's adaptive capacity. The findings demonstrate that women's empowerment is not positioned as a core pillar of climate resilience, resulting in adaptation strategies that insufficiently address intersecting vulnerabilities. The article argues that meaningful gender- responsive adaptation requires institutional reforms that embed intersectionality, strengthen women's agency in governance, and align climate action with broader socio-economic transformation goals. Policy recommendations include institutionalizing gender-responsive budgeting, enhancing participatory climate governance, and strengthening accountability mechanisms across national and local adaptation processes.

title: A snapshot of the current agroforestry organizational landscape in the United States focused on non-profit and university-based institutions
summary: Abstract Although agroforestry organizations exist across the United States and their numbers appear to be increasing, available information about their presence and growth is largely anecdotal. The composition of the agroforestry organizat
content: Abstract Although agroforestry organizations exist across the United States and their numbers appear to be increasing, available information about their presence and growth is largely anecdotal. The composition of the agroforestry organizational landscape in the US has not previously been described, and detailed, systematically collected data are not publicly available. This study aims to address this gap and explore the current distribution, qualities, and characteristics of agroforestry actors across the US. The study was conducted through a survey distributed across organizations identified as involved in agroforestry through existing network contacts and an open data search, focusing on those that extend beyond agroforestry farming practices alone. Descriptive statistics and comparative analysis were used to present the results and findings. This snapshot of the current agroforestry organizational landscape is depicted with 71 organizations who responded to our survey, including non-profit organizations (45%), university-based (24%), and for-profit (13%) organizations. The number of organizations involved in agroforestry has grown, especially in recent decades. Our findings showed agroforestry organizations present in 30 states, with the highest concentrations in the Midwest and Northeast regions. The non-profit sector plays an important role as a provider of full-time employment positions for agroforestry professionals, while government programs and foundations are major funders of agroforestry work. Funding was identified as both the key opportunity and the principal barrier to expanded agroforestry engagement. Key areas where organizations are focused include informal education, community building, exploration of alternative income opportunities for landowners/farmers, demonstration farms, and technical assistance. Among agroforestry practices, silvopasture is emphasized most among non-profits and university-based organizations, while alley cropping and forest farming are prioritized by for-profit, cooperatives, and coalitions. The results of this research present a cross-section of the current U.S. agroforestry organizational landscape, and they provide valuable baseline data for future research and policy directions.

title: VALORIZATION OF INDUSTRIAL FRUIT PROCESSING BY-PRODUCTS: TECHNOFUNCTIONAL PROPERTIES AND BIO-ENHANCEMENT VIA SUBMERGED LACTIC ACID FERMENTATION
summary: Fruit processing by-products are rich in functional compounds but underutilized in the development of food products. Therefore, with effective waste processing, high value-added products can be developed from these industrial by-products wi
content: Fruit processing by-products are rich in functional compounds but underutilized in the development of food products. Therefore, with effective waste processing, high value-added products can be developed from these industrial by-products within the framework of a circular economy. In this context, the aim of this study was to increase the antioxidant capacity of industrial apple, apricot, and peach pomaces through 48-hour submerged lactic acid fermentation and to investigate their technofunctional properties. Pre-treated apple, apricot, and peach pomace powders exhibited notable technofunctional properties, including water and oil holding capacities, swelling capacity, solubility, emulsifying activity index, and emulsion stability index. Fermentation increased total phenolic content (42.29-59.49%), cupric reducing antioxidant capacity (CUPRAC) (39.65-65.08%), and 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) radical scavenging activity (7.21-33.79%). The results demonstrate that industrial fruit wastes exhibit multiple technofunctional properties and that submerged lactic acid fermentation is an effective process to enhance bioactive potential.

title: Plasmalogen deficiency is associated with major polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) alterations in the mouse retina
summary: Background: Plasmalogens are ether-phospholipids that play essential roles in cell physiology. They serve as reservoirs for polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), which regulate retinal vascular development. Plasmalogen deficiency is associat
content: Background: Plasmalogens are ether-phospholipids that play essential roles in cell physiology. They serve as reservoirs for polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), which regulate retinal vascular development. Plasmalogen deficiency is associated with severe ocular defects in mice, including abnormal retinal vascularization. However, the impact of plasmalogen deficiency on retinal fatty acid composition remains to be determined. Objectives: This study evaluated the effects of plasmalogen deficiency on mouse retinal fatty acid composition and whether dietary supplementation of lactating mothers with a plasmalogen precursor, alkylglycerol, could prevent these alterations in offspring. Because the retina is an extension of the central nervous system, the brain cortex was also analyzed to compare tissue-specific responses to plasmalogen deficiency. Methods: Lactating mice were fed a diet enriched with 2% alkylglycerols. Retinal and brain fatty acid compositions were determined in pups at postnatal day 21 using gas chromatography with flame ionization detection (GC-FID). Results: Plasmalogen deficiency was associated with significant alterations in retinal fatty acid composition. Total PUFAs content was significantly reduced, while the n−6:n−3 ratio was strongly increased. These changes were accompanied by modest but significant increases in saturated and monounsaturated fatty acids. Alterations of PUFAs composition were also observed in the cortex. Maternal alkylglycerol supplementation showed only a slight trend toward improvement and was insufficient to restore retinal plasmalogen levels, PUFA content, or n−6:n−3 ratio. In the brain, alkylglycerol supplementation had no effect, suggesting potential tissue-specific differences in precursors uptake/metabolism.Conclusions: Plasmalogen deficiency significantly disrupts the fatty acid composition of the retina, primarily through PUFA depletion and an increased n−6:n−3 ratio. These alterations may contribute to the pathological retinal phenotype observed in plasmalogen-deficient mice. Maternal alkylglycerol supplementation during early postnatal life is insufficient to correct these defects. Further studies are needed to clarify the role of altered lipid composition in retinal vascular development.

title: Evolution from Traditional Dairy based Fermented Beverages to Emerging Plant-Based Alternatives
summary: Fermented beverages have received significant research and industry attention due to recent findings showing the association between consumption of these beverages and nutritional, functional, and medicinal benefits. Fermented beverages are
content: Fermented beverages have received significant research and industry attention due to recent findings showing the association between consumption of these beverages and nutritional, functional, and medicinal benefits. Fermented beverages are produced using various substrates including dairy, cereals, fruits, vegetables, legumes, nuts, and seeds through microbial fermentation resulting in beverages with probiotic and other functional ingredients, such as bioactives, antioxidants, vitamins, and minerals beneficial for human health. Moreover, fermentation brings a lot of value to the product due to extended shelf-life, enhanced sensory characteristics, increased digestibility and availability of nutrients, improved safety from microorganisms and pathogenic strains. There are various kinds of dairy fermented beverages including kefir, yogurt drinks, lassi, buttermilk, kumis, ayran known for their probiotic and nutritional value. However, cereal-based fermented drinks still remain an important part of the daily diets and food supply in many countries. Due to increasing cases of lactose intolerance and veganism, environmental sustainability, and preventive nutrition, there is a growing tendency to shift the demand from milk-based to plant-based fermented beverages. The fermentation method, bacteria utilized, qualities, health consequences, industrial practices, and future prospects of fermented beverages are all thoroughly reviewed in this paper, which covers both conventional and novel fermented beverages.

title: Energy communities foster solar energy diffusion and distributive justice: Insights from a System Dynamics transition model
summary: The diffusion of residential renewable technologies depends not only on technology costs and incentives, but also on interactions among technologies, household decisions, institutions, and access to collective business models. Existing tran
content: The diffusion of residential renewable technologies depends not only on technology costs and incentives, but also on interactions among technologies, household decisions, institutions, and access to collective business models. Existing transition models rarely combine these elements while evaluating their distributional implications. This study develops a socio-technical System Dynamics model of the Swiss residential sector to examine the long-term co-adoption of photovoltaic systems and heating technologies under heterogeneous cantonal regulations and alternative energy community designs. The model represents household adoption decisions and feedback involving public authorities, electric utilities, policy incentives, and electricity prices. Results show that the adoption of photovoltaic systems and heat pumps is strongly interlinked, indicating that policies addressing both technologies jointly can better account for their interdependence in transition pathways. Enabling energy communities increases photovoltaic deployment, particularly in multi-family buildings facing structural and economic barriers to individual adoption. Under the modeled incentive, tariff, and participation conditions, virtual energy communities also improve the two distributional indicators evaluated in the study by expanding access to decentralized electricity and reducing average levy payments for households in buildings without on-site photovoltaic systems. These findings show how energy-community regulation can influence technology diffusion and selected monetary and access-related distributional outcomes, while emphasizing that the effects depend on policy design and modeled assumptions.

title: Replication Data for “Water Resource Tax Reform and Corporate Green Investment”
summary: This merged dataset provides the firm-year-level data used to examine the effect of China’s water resource tax reform on corporate green investment. The dataset covers Chinese listed firms and combines the main regression data with the addi
content: This merged dataset provides the firm-year-level data used to examine the effect of China’s water resource tax reform on corporate green investment. The dataset covers Chinese listed firms and combines the main regression data with the additional variables used in the robustness tests, mechanism analysis, heterogeneity analysis, and extended analysis. It includes corporate green investment variables, policy treatment indicators, the triple-difference treatment variable, firm-level controls, industry and regional identifiers, financing variables, managerial and environmental characteristics, and variables related to the economic and environmental consequences examined in the associated manuscript. The dataset is provided to facilitate replication of the empirical analyses reported in the associated manuscript. Variable names are presented in English and correspond to the terminology used in the manuscript. The data were compiled from publicly available statistical sources and licensed financial databases; users should comply with the terms of the original data providers when reusing the data.

title: The impact of ESG peer pressure on corporate green transformation under dual horizontal and vertical networks
summary: This study examines the impact of ESG peer pressure on corporate green transformation and its underlying mechanisms within horizontal and vertical networks, using non-financial enterprises listed on China's A-share market from 2009 to 2023
content: This study examines the impact of ESG peer pressure on corporate green transformation and its underlying mechanisms within horizontal and vertical networks, using non-financial enterprises listed on China's A-share market from 2009 to 2023 as the research sample. Findings reveal that horizontal ESG peer pressure promotes green transformation: when other firms in an industry exhibit generally superior ESG performance, it encourages the target firm to pursue green transformation actively. Vertical ESG peer pressure similarly drives green transformation: when other enterprises in a company's supply chain demonstrate superior overall ESG performance, it encourages the firm to pursue green transformation actively.
