title: An Exploration of Mechanochemical Activation on Various Potential Supplementary Cementitious Materials
source: Journal of the American Ceramic Society
summary: ABSTRACT The use of supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) is a major way to reduce the carbon footprint of concrete. Mechanochemical activation (MCA) can be used to activate inert materials that can then be used as SCMs. In this study
content: ABSTRACT The use of supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) is a major way to reduce the carbon footprint of concrete. Mechanochemical activation (MCA) can be used to activate inert materials that can then be used as SCMs. In this study, the effect of MCA using a planetary ball mill was investigated for 16 materials, ranging from natural occurring materials to by‐products from various industries. In general, MCA caused the formation of nanoparticles, which were aggregated (rigidly bound) and agglomerated (loosely bound). Increased particle sphericity was also observed from scanning electron microscopy data. Additionally, the amorphous content, Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) specific surface area, and total pore volume increased for after MCA respectively by 29%, 172%, and 427% on average. We demonstrated that initially reactive materials show modest increases (92% average increase) in reactivity after MCA. In contrast, inert materials experience a much greater increase (1126% average increase) depending on their chemical composition, amorphous content, BET specific surface area, and phase hardness. From the tested materials, all initially inert ones were transformed into reactive SCMs after MCA. Under the same MCA grinding conditions, pre‐MCA reactivity can be used to predict post‐MCA reactivity.

title: Stratification-induced hypoxia shapes greenhouse gas dynamics in ponds
summary: Abstract. Fresh waters in general and ponds in particular are biogeochemical hot spots and as such are sources of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, especially methane (CH4) and carbon dioxide (CO2). Several studies have shown that thermal str
content: Abstract. Fresh waters in general and ponds in particular are biogeochemical hot spots and as such are sources of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, especially methane (CH4) and carbon dioxide (CO2). Several studies have shown that thermal stratification of the water column is a common characteristic of ponds, but how this process influences GHG dynamics is less well studied. We tracked thermal stratification and the associated hypoxia in six ponds across the growing season and measured dissolved CH4 and CO2 in surface and bottom waters, along with CH4 ebullition, every two weeks. The results showed that all ponds stratified during the growing season and that thermal stratification often, but not always, led to bottom-water hypoxia. Where hypoxia occurred, bottom-water CH4 was approximately 16 times higher (median 3.05 vs 0.19 mg C L−1), CO2 about 3 times higher (11.6 vs 4.03 mg C L−1) and CH4 ebullition was about 3.4 times higher than in oxic conditions. In contrast, surface-water GHG concentrations showed no significant difference between periods with and without bottom-water hypoxia. Bottom-water temperatures were not significantly different between hypoxic and oxic states, indicating oxygen availability, rather than temperature, dominated GHG buildup and ebullition. Stratification and the resulting hypoxia enhance CH4 ebullition and promote high concentrations of GHGs in bottom waters, which may be released in small or larger pulses as the water column mixes partially or fully. In summary this study demonstrates that thermal stratification, by inducing bottom-water hypoxia, strongly influences the GHG dynamics across a range of timescales in ponds.

title: A Comprehensive Understanding of CO <sub>2</sub> Emissions from Hybrid Vehicles Using Long Short-Term Memory
source: Transportation Research Record Journal of the Transportation Research Board
summary: Insufficient exploration of hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) in relation to carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions may lead to significant policy-related problems. Previous studies emphasize comparisons between internal combustion engine vehicles
content: Insufficient exploration of hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) in relation to carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions may lead to significant policy-related problems. Previous studies emphasize comparisons between internal combustion engine vehicles and HEVs, rather than an exclusive focus on HEVs. A detailed investigation of HEV-derived CO 2 emissions is needed to understand their emission profiles across different road types. Moreover, the limited existing studies on HEV emissions have not considered trip lengths and spatial attributes, which are essential factors considering the operating functions of HEVs. This study aims to fill this gap by integrating data of engine characteristics, trip lengths, and spatial attributes of road types to assess the impact of these factors on CO 2 emissions using a real-world, second-by-second vehicle energy data set. A deep learning framework, long short-term memory model, is employed to predict the CO 2 emissions of HEVs. Permutation feature importance is used to quantify the relative importance of key predictors. Fuel consumption, mass air flow, trip lengths, and spatial attributes emerged as the key predictors of the model. To better explore the relationship between key predictors and CO 2 emissions, we also visualized their distributions. The results revealed that CO 2 emissions increase significantly with higher speed. Motorways generally involve longer trips, resulting in higher CO 2 emissions than short trips, despite a significant difference in the proportion of trips. Short trips tend to emit more CO 2 on local roads. The findings from this data-driven modeling study have practical implications in the transportation sector.

title: Inclusive governance and sustainable development challenges in solar radiation management
content: Solar Radiation Management (SRM) is increasingly attracting attention in scientific and policy discussions due to its potential to partially offset anthropogenic climate change. At the same time, SRM raises major governance, ethical, and sustainable development challenges, particularly regarding legitimacy, participation, and unequal institutional capacities between countries. While research and governance discussions continue to expand, actors from the Global North (GN) remain dominant in agenda-setting and decision-making processes, whereas the Global South (GS), despite its disproportionate vulnerability to climate impacts, remains comparatively underrepresented. This article examines SRM governance through the lens of inclusive governance and sustainable development. It argues that governance arrangements lacking transparency, accountability, and equitable participation risk reinforcing existing inequalities in global environmental governance and undermining Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 13 (Climate Action), SDG 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities), and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals). Drawing on a qualitative literature review and a case study of the SRM Non-Use Agreement, the article analyzes the evolution of SRM debates and the structural factors shaping participation in governance discussions. Recent institutional assessments, including the United Nations Environment (UNEP) Program Solar Radiation Modification Working Paper further highlight major governance gaps, scientific uncertainty, and asymmetries in research capacity between developed and developing countries. The analysis explores governance mechanisms capable of strengthening transparency, participation, and ethical safeguards in emerging SRM governance frameworks. Beyond documenting existing governance gaps, this article makes three contributions. First, it combines a structured literature review with an empirical analysis of the SRM Non-Use Agreement to examine participation asymmetries. Second, it identifies the institutional factors that continue to constrain meaningful Global South participation in emerging SRM governance debates. Third, it proposes governance mechanisms that translate principles of inclusive governance and sustainable development into operational pathways for future SRM governance.

title: Reduction of CO₂ Emissions and Energy Consumption through Cement Minimization in Cement–Plastic Composite Masonry Blocks
summary: The cement industry is responsible for approximately 7–8% of global anthropogenic CO₂ emissions, primarily due to high-temperature clinker production and intensive energy consumption. Reducing cement content in construction materials repres
content: The cement industry is responsible for approximately 7–8% of global anthropogenic CO₂ emissions, primarily due to high-temperature clinker production and intensive energy consumption. Reducing cement content in construction materials represents a critical pathway toward sustainable development. This study evaluates the environmental benefits of lightweight masonry blocks produced with reduced cement content and recycled plastic aggregates. By replacing a significant portion of mineral aggregates and minimizing cement dosage to approximately 10–20%, the proposed composite block achieves notable reductions in embodied energy and CO₂ emissions. Analytical estimations demonstrate that cement reduction directly lowers process-related emissions while recycled plastic utilization diverts waste from landfills. The results confirm that environmental performance can be improved without compromising structural or thermal requirements, offering a viable solution for low-carbon construction.

title: DETERMINAN TAX AVOIDANCE DENGAN CARBON EMISSION SEBAGAI PEMODERASI PADA PERUSAHAAN ENERGI & PERTAMBANGAN
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Komisaris Independen, Profitabilitas, dan Capital Intensity terhadap Tax Avoidance, dengan Carbon Emission sebagai variabel pemoderasi, pada perusahaan sektor energi dan pertambangan yang
content: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Komisaris Independen, Profitabilitas, dan Capital Intensity terhadap Tax Avoidance, dengan Carbon Emission sebagai variabel pemoderasi, pada perusahaan sektor energi dan pertambangan yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2020–2024. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan data sekunder berupa laporan keuangan tahunan, dan teknik purposive sampling yang menghasilkan 320 sampel data olahan. Analisis data dilakukan melalui uji statistik deskriptif, uji asumsi klasik, uji regresi linear berganda, dan uji regresi moderasi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Komisaris Independen dan Capital Intensity tidak berpengaruh terhadap Tax Avoidance, sedangkan Profitabilitas berpengaruh positif terhadap Tax Avoidance. Carbon Emission terbukti memperlemah pengaruh Komisaris Independen dan Profitabilitas terhadap Tax Avoidance, namun tidak mampu memoderasi pengaruh Capital Intensity. Temuan ini mengindikasikan bahwa keberadaan komisaris independen pada perusahaan sampel masih bersifat formalitas regulasi, sementara tingkat pengungkapan emisi karbon yang tinggi mendorong perusahaan untuk lebih transparan dan patuh secara pajak akibat tekanan legitimasi dari pemangku kepentingan. Penelitian ini memberikan implikasi penting bagi regulator dan pelaku usaha dalam merancang kebijakan tata kelola dan transparansi lingkungan yang lebih efektif guna mendorong kepatuhan pajak di sektor energi dan pertambangan.

title: Green human resource management in tourism and hospitality: theory and impact-driven analysis
source: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Insights
summary: Purpose This study offers a systematic review of green human resource management (GHRM) in the hospitality and tourism settings, critically synthesizing and evaluating 178 peer-reviewed articles published between 2014 and 2024 to clarify th
content: Purpose This study offers a systematic review of green human resource management (GHRM) in the hospitality and tourism settings, critically synthesizing and evaluating 178 peer-reviewed articles published between 2014 and 2024 to clarify theoretical development and identify key research gaps in the field. Design/methodology/approach Following the PRISMA protocol, the study employs a transparent, replicable review process to examine the theoretical foundations, methodological orientations and multilevel impacts of GHRM in this labor-intensive, service-based sector. Findings The findings reveal that the ability-motivation-opportunity (AMO) framework and the resource-based view (RBV) are the dominant theoretical perspectives underpinning GHRM research in hospitality. Supported by other theories, employees emerge as central mediators translating GHRM initiatives into environmental outcomes and service experiences, thus positioning human capital as a valuable, rare, inimitable and non-substitutable (VRIN) resource. The review also identifies key theoretical, methodological and contextual limitations in the existing literature to guide future research. Practical implications The review suggests that managers should implement GHRM as an integrated strategic system and prioritize employees' role as the primary mechanism for creating sustainable organizational and customer value. Policymakers and regulators can further facilitate GHRM adoption through standardized implementation guidelines and certification frameworks. Originality/value This study moves beyond descriptive prior reviews by developing a more analytically grounded and integrative multilevel framework of GHRM impacts, explaining how complementary theoretical perspectives collectively account for the mechanisms through which GHRM creates value across levels. By clarifying the central role of employees in this GHRM outcome model, the review suggests reconceptualizing GHRM as a human-centered transformation process rather than merely a collection of green HR practices.

title: Carbon footprint
summary: A carbon footprint is a calculation of the total greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions resulting from an activity and is based on Life Cycle Assessment calculations. The metric is measured in kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent (kg CO2 eq). The
content: A carbon footprint is a calculation of the total greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions resulting from an activity and is based on Life Cycle Assessment calculations. The metric is measured in kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent (kg CO2 eq). The carbon footprint consists of two components: direct and indirect GHG emissions. For accounting and reporting purposes, the GHG Protocol further differentiates these GHG emissions into Scope 1, 2, and 3 based on their sources. Carbon footprint can be assessed at the product level, namely, Product Carbon Footprint (PCF), to facilitate data-driven, low-carbon product designs and support informed decision-making for consumers purchasing products with low environmental impacts. On a corporate level, Corporate Carbon Footprint (CCF) assists in identifying climate risks and influencing the development of corporate sustainability strategies to meet compliance requirements. Understanding and analysing carbon footprints is essential for identifying areas of improvement, implementing mitigation strategies against climate change, and promoting sustainable transition.

title: A Study on the Energy Consumption of Blockchain Consensus Mechanisms
source: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science
summary: Blockchain technology has become a strong backbone to decentralized applications; however, the fast-growing energy usage of consensus mechanisms has become a cause of serious economic, environmental, and sustainability worries. This paper w
content: Blockchain technology has become a strong backbone to decentralized applications; however, the fast-growing energy usage of consensus mechanisms has become a cause of serious economic, environmental, and sustainability worries. This paper will be a detailed examination of the energy usage in the leading blockchain consensus algorithms, focusing specifically on the question of why some of them are high-energy usage and how their energy imprints might be decreased. The paper has started by conducting a review of the basic architecture of blockchain systems and classifying the different consensus mechanisms according to their working principle and resource needs. To analyze energy-intensive schemes, the specific attention is paid to Proof of Work, which is analyzed in terms of models of mining operations, hardware dependence, difficulty adjustment, and power consumption. Case studies of large-scaled PoW-based blockchains are presented in real-life scenarios to represent the implications of the energy in practical scenarios and network conditions. Moreover, the research also undertakes the systematic examination of optimization methods that will help to decrease the energy consumption without affecting the security or decentralization. These are innovations at the protocol level, hardware-awareness, mining policies based on renewable energy sources, and the use of layer-2 and off-chain transaction processing systems. Trade-offs between security, scalability, and decentralization and energy efficiency are discussed comparatively. The findings show that next-generation consensus mechanisms and hybrid designs are capable of saving a huge amount of energy without compromising the reasonable performance and trust guarantees.

title: Analysis of structural and functional characteristics of co-assembled complexes of walnut protein isolate and whey protein isolate
summary: To address low utilization of protein-based by-products in food processing and meet growing demand for high-quality protein materials. This study prepared complexes using pH cycling and co-assembly with walnut protein isolate (WNPI) and whe
content: To address low utilization of protein-based by-products in food processing and meet growing demand for high-quality protein materials. This study prepared complexes using pH cycling and co-assembly with walnut protein isolate (WNPI) and whey protein isolate (WPI), systematically investigate the structural characteristics, functional characteristics, and the structure-function relationship. Results showed significant enhancements in solubility, emulsifying capacity, foaming ability, and particle stability of the complexes. These advancements were linked to protein structural rearrangements induced by pH changes, leading to smaller particle sizes, strengthened electrostatic interactions, and greater surface hydrophobicity. This not only relaxed the rigid structure of the protein but also improved the molecular flexibility of the protein. A network of intricate forces, such as hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions, electrostatic interactions, and disulfide bonds, preserved the stability of the protein molecules. This study aims to address WNPI stability issues, promote innovative development of protein by-products, and provide a theoretical foundation for exploring plant-animal protein co-assembly composites.

title: From DNA-Encoded Chemistry to Tumor-Targeted Small Molecule Therapeutics
summary: Unlike conventional screening methods, which are limited by library size, DNA-encoded chemical library (DEL) technology enables the simultaneous interrogation of billions of compounds, each uniquely barcoded with DNA tags. These libraries c
content: Unlike conventional screening methods, which are limited by library size, DNA-encoded chemical library (DEL) technology enables the simultaneous interrogation of billions of compounds, each uniquely barcoded with DNA tags. These libraries can be screened through affinity-based capture and decoded using high-throughput sequencing. DEL-derived ligands can be conjugated to cytotoxic agents or radioactive isotopes, facilitating the creation of highly selective therapeutics that target diseased cells while minimizing off-target effects. This article explores the use of DELs for identifying high-affinity small organic ligands for the development of small molecule–radio conjugates (SMRCs) and small molecule–drug conjugates (SMDCs).

title: A feasibility study of vibrational spectroscopy methods for greenhouse gas detection at the “Rossyanka” Carbon Measurement Supersite (Kaliningrad Oblast, Russia)
source: Scientific and technical journal of information technologies mechanics and optics
summary: The paper presents the results of an investigation that employed vibrational spectroscopy as a monitoring technique for greenhouse gases at the “Rossyanka” Carbon Measurement Supersite, in Kaliningrad Oblast. The application of these method
content: The paper presents the results of an investigation that employed vibrational spectroscopy as a monitoring technique for greenhouse gases at the “Rossyanka” Carbon Measurement Supersite, in Kaliningrad Oblast. The application of these methodologies is indicative of their efficacy in the quantitative detection of greenhouse gases, with a particular focus on carbon dioxide (CO2). The capacity of infrared (IR) and Raman spectroscopy (RS) for the monitoring of O2 in field conditions is illustrated, with a discrepancy of approximately 100 ppm observed between the calculated and experimental values of concentrations in field samples. Methods of IR and RS using a Virsa (Renishaw) and Shimadzu IRPrestige 21 spectrometer have been applied. The survey was carried out by recording the spectra of gases sealed in a glass vial for medicines with a volume of 10 ml. The obtained samples of the spectra of the gas mixture were compared with the spectra of a reference sample with a known concentration. The results demonstrate the feasibility of using IR and RS wile determine greenhouse gas concentrations at carbon supersites throughout the country, including the “Rossyanka” Carbon Measurement Supersite where CO2 concentrations can be determined with a registration threshold of 300500 ppm and the isolation of the main characteristic vibrational modes. For the samples obtained at the “Rossyanka” Carbon Measurement Supersite, the applied vibrational spectroscopy methods enabled the quantification of only the concentration of CO2. The presence of CH4 was not detected in the samples due to the low concentrations of the gas which were found to be as low as 10 ppm according to gas chromatography. It is expected that further studies using signal amplification methods, such as using multi-pass cuvettes, will solve this problem when registering low greenhouse gas concentrations. It is expected that further studies using signal amplification methods, such as using multi-pass cuvettes and RS, will solve this problem when registering low greenhouse gas concentrations.

title: Economic Growth, Energy Consumption, and Environmental Sustainability in Southeast Asia: Evidence from Symmetric and Asymmetric Models
summary: This study examines the effects of economic growth and energy consumption on environmental degradation in nine Southeast Asian countries from 1990 to 2022. By jointly employing carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions and the ecological footprint (EF
content: This study examines the effects of economic growth and energy consumption on environmental degradation in nine Southeast Asian countries from 1990 to 2022. By jointly employing carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions and the ecological footprint (EFP) within both symmetric and asymmetric panel ARDL frameworks, the study provides a more comprehensive assessment of environmental sustainability than previous studies that rely on a single environmental indicator or a linear specification. The empirical results indicate that economic growth and energy consumption remain key drivers of environmental degradation, although their effects vary with the environmental indicator used. Both the panel ARDL and NARDL estimates support the EKC hypothesis when environmental degradation is measured by CO2 emissions, but reject it when the EFP is used, highlighting the importance of adopting multidimensional measures of environmental sustainability. Furthermore, the panel NARDL results reveal significant long-run asymmetric effects of energy consumption, with increases in energy use exerting stronger adverse impacts on both CO2 emissions and the EFP than equivalent decreases. These contrasting findings suggest that improvements in carbon efficiency associated with economic growth do not necessarily alleviate broader pressures on natural resources and ecological systems. The robustness of the results is confirmed using FMOLS, DOLS, and CCR estimators, while the causality analysis identifies long-run bidirectional relationships among economic growth, energy consumption, and environmental degradation. These findings emphasize the need for integrated policy measures that promote renewable energy adoption, cleaner industrial development, improved energy efficiency, and stronger environmental governance to support sustainable economic growth and accelerate the transition toward net-zero emissions in Southeast Asia.

title: Paludiculture - a scoping review of the agricultural, economic and social science literature
summary: Introduction Paludiculture has emerged as a science-initiated land use concept for wet peatlands more than 25 years ago. While research accumulates especially for natural science topics, a recent synthesis for agricultural, economic and soc
content: Introduction Paludiculture has emerged as a science-initiated land use concept for wet peatlands more than 25 years ago. While research accumulates especially for natural science topics, a recent synthesis for agricultural, economic and social science topics is lacking. We review agricultural, economic, and social science literature on paludiculture with three goals: (1) to explore the current extent and status of this literature and the use of paludiculture definitions, (2) to identify major research gaps for the thematic areas establishment and crop production, planning and approval, utilization, economics and socio-economics, and (3) to derive research implications from practical recommendations for transformation to sustainable peatland use and paludiculture. Methods A scoping review was conducted following a structured literature search with the search string “paludicult*” in Web of Science and Scopus. After screening, the literature body was further analyzed using a codebook with predefined assessment criteria as well as qualitative data analysis techniques. Results The database of 231 publications shows a substantial amount of predominantly interdisciplinary peer-reviewed literature over time, with a large share of experiments and case studies dealing with one or multiple paludiculture plants/land uses, as well as overarching conceptual studies. Most literature originates in Europe, while also in Asia, predominantly Indonesia, a distinct literature stream is emerging. Definitions mainly establish a relation between terms referring to land use, peatland or organic soils and water table, while also misconceptions of the paludiculture concept were identified. Research gaps specific for the thematic areas pertain, e.g., to quantitative survey studies in economics and socio-economics or value chain perspectives in utilization. Discussion Based on this review, we recommend to increase agricultural, economic and social research on current land use on (wet) peatlands, establish more long-term and large-scale demonstration sites on diverse paludicultures enabling interdisciplinary research and to intensify attempts for overarching data syntheses and meta-analyses, to draw further comprehensive and knowledge-based recommendations to support practical paludiculture implementation.

title: Education form Below Stustainable Livelihoods and Clean Energy Transition Dilemmas in Tanzania
source: ZEP – Zeitschrift für internationale Bildungsforschung und Entwicklungspädagogik
summary: Afrika hat als Reaktion auf den Klimawandel den Übergang zu sauberer Energie eingeleitet, um Bäume zu schützen, die für Holzkohle und Brennholz gefällt werden. Doch während die Gründe für die Energiewende in politischen Dokumenten gut formu
content: Afrika hat als Reaktion auf den Klimawandel den Übergang zu sauberer Energie eingeleitet, um Bäume zu schützen, die für Holzkohle und Brennholz gefällt werden. Doch während die Gründe für die Energiewende in politischen Dokumenten gut formuliert sein mögen, gibt es kaum Forschungsarbeiten, die die Reaktionen der Menschen auf die Energiewende untersuchen sowie die Herausforderungen, denen sie täglich bei der Bewältigung und Aushandlung von Energiezugang und -erschwinglichkeit gegenüberstehen. Dieser Beitrag diskutiert Ergebnisse einer in Tansania durchgeführten qualitativen Untersuchung. Der Beitrag kommt zu dem Schluss, dass die Energiewende von vier Faktoren abhängt, nämlich Bildung von unten, wirtschaftlicher Stärkung, politischem Wille und von Umweltgerechtigkeit.

title: Sustainable Smart Tour Routing: An Integrated Framework for Destination Management in Sangkhlaburi District, Thailand
source: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science
summary: Environmental degradation, the concentration of visitors at tourism destinations, the negative impacts of transport on the environment, and the unbalanced distribution of the benefits of tourism are among the challenges faced by tourism des
content: Environmental degradation, the concentration of visitors at tourism destinations, the negative impacts of transport on the environment, and the unbalanced distribution of the benefits of tourism are among the challenges faced by tourism destinations. Although the routining of tours is traditionally considered an operational task, this study suggests that it could be a strategic tool in sustainable destination management. The quantitative, cross-sectional survey consisted of 400 tourists visiting Sangkhlaburi District, Kanchanaburi Province, Thailand, to investigate the integration of environmental, economic, social, and technological aspects of sustainability into tour route design. The findings reveal significant relationships between sustainable tour routing, sustainable tourism activities, service quality and tourist satisfaction. Sustainable tourist routes developed around community participation, resource conservation, and smart tourism technologies are more sustainable and beneficial in terms of experience gain than traditional tourist routes focusing on attraction development. A sustainable smart tour routing framework, combining the analysis of GIS, artificial intelligence, and destination sustainability indices, is proposed in five stages. This study brings sustainable tourism theory to the operational level of route planning and provides suggestions for tourism operators, destination managers, and policymakers.

title: Pore Structure Characterization of Sugar-Derived Carbon: A Mul-ti-Dimensional Analysis via X-ray Micro-CT and Avizo
summary: Abstract Sugar-hydrogel pyrolysis (SHP) provides a cost-effective route for producing high-performance struc-tural carbon from biomass, yet how sol formulation and processing parameters regulate the pore struc-ture of sugar-derived carbon r
content: Abstract Sugar-hydrogel pyrolysis (SHP) provides a cost-effective route for producing high-performance struc-tural carbon from biomass, yet how sol formulation and processing parameters regulate the pore struc-ture of sugar-derived carbon remains insufficiently understood.Using X-ray micro-CT and three-dimensional quantitative analysis in Avizo software, this study investigates how acrylamide (AM) concentration, N,N'-methylenebisacrylamide (MBA) concentration, sugar concentration, sugar type, and carbonization temperature regulates the pore structure of sugar-derived carbon. Results indicate that AM and MBA, as the key building units of the gel skeleton, govern the primary pore framework and enable precise control over pore size distribution, respectively. Sugar concentration adjusts pore size distribution through a competitive mechanism between precursor packing density and volatile yield during pyrolysis. The influence of sugar type depends on the temporal correspondence between its py-rolysis temperature window and gel skeleton shrinkage, which directly determines the intrinsic pore characteristics. Heat treatment temperature promotes the transformation from isolated closed pores to an interconnected network through the synergy between carbon skeleton shrinkage and microcrack bridging. This work provides theoretical insight and experimental evidence for multi-parameter regula-tion of pore structure in sugar-derived carbon.

title: Structural effects of alcohols on H₂S solubility and thermodynamic modeling of binary mixtures with benzyl alcohol, phenol, and ethanol
summary: The solubility of hydrogen sulfide in benzyl alcohol, phenol, and ethanol was experimentally investigated at low to medium pressures over temperature ranges of 313.15–353.15 K, 318.15–353.15 K, and 303.15–333.15 K, respectively. The results
content: The solubility of hydrogen sulfide in benzyl alcohol, phenol, and ethanol was experimentally investigated at low to medium pressures over temperature ranges of 313.15–353.15 K, 318.15–353.15 K, and 303.15–333.15 K, respectively. The results were compared with literature data for methanol, propanol, butanol, ethylene glycol, diethylene glycol, triethylene glycol, and thiodiglycol to study the effect of molecular structure on H₂S absorption. The experimental data were obtained using a static method and were correlated using two modeling approaches: (1) a thermodynamic approach using the Peng–Robinson–Stryjek–Vera (PRSV) equation of state with the Panagiotopoulos–Reid (PR) mixing rule, and (2) a genetic programming (GP) approach. The average and maximum relative deviations ( ARD / MRD %) for the PRSV/PR EoS are 0.96/3.04% for benzyl alcohol, 1.72/8.07% for phenol, and 1.03/4.79% for ethanol, respectively. For the genetic programming approach, these values are 3.24/20.38%, 6.38/30.19%, and 4.43/21.30%, respectively, indicating that the PRSV/PR model produces superior results compared to the GP model. The solubility trend of H₂S in the studied alcohols, diols, and triols follows the order: TEG > phenol > DEG ≈ benzyl alcohol > butanol ≈ thiodiglycol > propanol > methanol > ethanol > propanediol > ethanediol.

title: Phenological phases of two early-maturing sweetpotato (Ipomoea batatas [L.] Lam.) cultivars
summary: Introduction. In Cuba, only general descriptions of sweetpotato phenology have been documented, without detailed information for producers and researchers. Objective. To characterize the main phenological phases of two early-maturing sweetp
content: Introduction. In Cuba, only general descriptions of sweetpotato phenology have been documented, without detailed information for producers and researchers. Objective. To characterize the main phenological phases of two early-maturing sweetpotato cultivars (Ipomoea batatas [L.] Lam.) under Cuban conditions. Materials and methods. A randomized complete block design with 10 replicates per cultivar was conducted at the Research Institute of Tropical Roots and Tuber Crops (INIVIT), Cuba. Two early cultivars from the INIVIT breeding program were evaluated: CEMSA 78-354 and INIVIT B-50. Evaluations were performed every seven days from 2 to 128 days after planting (DAP). Results. Plant tubering initiation began at 28 DAP for both cultivars. In the final phase (100 - 128 DAP), CEMSA 78-354 increased yield by 14.18 t·ha⁻¹ and INIVIT B-50 by 11.84 t·ha⁻¹. From 86 DAP onward, Degrees Brix (°Bx) remained stable until harvest. The greatest increase in dry matter content occurred between 51 and 107 DAP: from 15.9% to 26.4% in CEMSA 78-354, and from 16.6% to 26.9% in INIVIT B-50. At 128 DAP, dry matter reached 28.15% (± 0.72) and 27.07% (± 1.11), respectively. Conclusion. In the second half of the cycle, CEMSA 78-354 allocated 63.1% (0.96 kg ± 0.13) of accumulated weight to tuberous roots, while INIVIT B-50 allocated 46.9% (1.08 kg ± 0.24). Three well-defined phenological phases are proposed for Ipomoea batatas: rooting (0-28 DAP), growth (29-65 DAP), and accumulation (66-128 DAP).

title: Tailoring Precise Genomic Integration Toward Isolate-to-Industry Strain Development for Scalable High-Titer Production of Polyhydroxyalkanoate
summary: Halophilic chassis has emerged as a promising biomanufacturing platform for industrial polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) production. However, challenges still remain in improving the production capacity, scalability and robustness, thereby lowerin
content: Halophilic chassis has emerged as a promising biomanufacturing platform for industrial polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) production. However, challenges still remain in improving the production capacity, scalability and robustness, thereby lowering cost to meet market demands. Here, a high-performing halophilic strain Halomonas LY03 was isolated with over 38% glucose-to-PHA conversion rate and broad non-grain substrate utilization capability. Multidimensional tools, including algorithm-guided high-expression neutral integration site (HENIS) screening toolkit designated 'SiteSeek', stop codon (TAA)-dependent enhancement of gene expression and recombinase-mediated large-fragment (> 9 kb) genomic integration, were then developed to enable precise, efficient and interference-free genomic integrative expression. Using these tools, various chromosomally engineered strains were rapidly constructed to achieve high-level production of poly-3-hydroxybutyrate (PHB, 151 g L-1) and poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-4-hydroxybutyrate) (P34HB, 139 g L-1) under high cell-density fermentation (up to 186 g L-1 cell dry weight) in a 5-L bioreactor. Scalability was demonstrated at 2-m3 and 20-m3 industry-scale fermentations, yielding up to 134 g L-1 PHB and 127 g L-1 P34HB (6.1 mol% 4HB). Building on the proven robustness, a two-stage continuous fermentation (TCF) process was developed using a twin-bioreactor system at 5-L and 20-m3 scales, where stable and sustained PHA production lasted over 260 h and 160 h, respectively. Techno-economic analysis revealed a substantial cost-reduction space of 48% compared with conventional fed-batch process. This study demonstrates a successful paradigm for engineering a newly isolated strain toward robust, high-titer and cost-competitive PHA production across lab-industry scales.

title: Encapsulation of pomegranate peel bioactive phenolic extract: laboratory proof-of-concept experiment, scale-up computer-aided batch process design, techno-economic feasibility and life cycle analysis
summary: Despite the proven antioxidant potential of Pomegranate Peel Extract (PPE), the lack of scalable, cost-effective, and systematically optimized processes for encapsulating PPE hinders its industrial application. This study presents an integr
content: Despite the proven antioxidant potential of Pomegranate Peel Extract (PPE), the lack of scalable, cost-effective, and systematically optimized processes for encapsulating PPE hinders its industrial application. This study presents an integrated laboratory proof-of-concept experiment, computer-aided batch process scale-up simulation, techno-economic assessment (TEA), and life cycle analysis (LCA) of PP bioactive phenolic extract microencapsulation via freeze-drying using a binary Gum Arabic and Maltodextrin wall system. Aspen Batch Process Developer (ABPD) was employed to simulate and scale the process across three production scenarios: mini-pilot (5 kg/day, Case 1), pilot-scale (100 kg/day, Case 2) and industrial-scale (5,000 kg/day, Case 3. The results were validated against experimental data with negligible deviation (MSE = 0.0001; MAPE = 0.06%). Physicochemical characterization confirmed high solubility (96.12%), low water activity (0.28), partial hygroscopicity (12.57%), and strong antioxidant capacity, collectively confirming functional stability for food and nutraceutical applications. TEA revealed progressive economic improvement with scale: Case 3 achieved the highest NPV ($18 million), the lowest levelized cost of production ($7.08/kg), and a strong IRR (53.9%). In contrast, Cases 1 and 2, which represented lower-scale setups, yielded lower NPVs and higher production costs. Monte Carlo simulation ( N = 10,000) identified selling price and annual production cost as the dominant profitability drivers, with Case 2 emerging as the most risk-adjusted investment pathway, achieving P(NPV > 0) of 91.9%. The LCA revealed that electrical energy consumption dominated environmental impacts. Freeze-drying alone accounted for 74.7–77.3% of total burdens and drove a GWP of 84.17 kg CO₂-eq per kg PPEP, highlighting energy management as the primary sustainability hotspot.

title: Plant–microbe interactions as drivers of sustainable agriculture: molecular mechanisms, stress mitigation, and future prospects
summary: Plant–microbe interaction is an essential component of sustainable agriculture which promotes plant growth, improves nutrient assimilation, and enhances plant resistance to various environmental stress conditions. Beneficial microbes, such
content: Plant–microbe interaction is an essential component of sustainable agriculture which promotes plant growth, improves nutrient assimilation, and enhances plant resistance to various environmental stress conditions. Beneficial microbes, such as rhizobacteria, mycorrhizal fungi, and endophytes, boost plant functions using molecular signaling, phytohormone modification, systemic resistance induction, and pathogen antagonism. The use of new multi-omics techniques has uncovered complicated communication systems mediated by root exudates, recognition via receptors and microbial community functioning. In this review, the current understanding of the molecular basis of plant–microbe associations and their roles in combating drought, salinity, temperature, and heavy metals stresses is summarized. Special attention is paid to the promising approach based on microbiome engineering, synthetic communities and next generation biofertilizers for climate-smart agriculture. The main difficulties associated with environmental fluctuations, host specificity, inconsistency at field scale, and the lack of omics and bioinoculant validation guidelines are also highlighted.

title: THE RUSSIAN CARBON UNITS MARKET IN THE CONTEXT OF CORSIA: FIRST STEPS TOWARDS INTERNATIONAL COMPATIBILITY
summary: Russia has already established a system for the circulation of carbon units, which includes rules for registering climate projects, the procedure for issuing and offsetting carbon units, and a national registry of carbon units, but its inte
content: Russia has already established a system for the circulation of carbon units, which includes rules for registering climate projects, the procedure for issuing and offsetting carbon units, and a national registry of carbon units, but its international component is still under development. This article examines the current state of the Russian carbon unit market in the context of the requirements of the international CORSIA mechanism, which is used in civil aviation to compensate for the increase in greenhouse gas emissions. To assess the readiness of the Russian carbon unit market to meet the requirements of CORSIA, a compatibility index has been calculated, which includes regulatory, registry, methodological, verification, and market components. The convergence of the Russian carbon unit market and CORSIA is possible through a comprehensive approach to legislative changes, improved project quality, and active interdepartmental cooperation.

title: Corporate carbon footprint
summary: The Corporate Carbon Footprint (CFF) reflects and reports on the sum of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions which are emitted directly or indirectly by a company or organization along the whole value chain. It covers emissions of people, service
content: The Corporate Carbon Footprint (CFF) reflects and reports on the sum of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions which are emitted directly or indirectly by a company or organization along the whole value chain. It covers emissions of people, services, or products over a certain period. A CCF calculation can serve various purposes. It creates the transparency needed to discover emissions reduction opportunities for organizations. It also helps identify the most relevant climate risks and opportunities for organizations and their business. The CCF is an important assessment and carbon accounting management approach to accurately report all relevant GHG emissions of a company, upstream and downstream. It covers direct emissions and indirect emissions. Measuring and tracking CFF creates information that is important to interested parties (stakeholders) and supports their decisions.

title: Environmental Management System (ISO 14001) and Total‐Factor Carbon Emission Performance: A Two‐Stage Malmquist Data Envelopment Analysis
summary: ABSTRACT As global decarbonization goals become more urgent, it is vital to understand that decoupling carbon from growth is not a purely mechanical process of adopting green machines; it is a socio‐technical transition. Understanding carbo
content: ABSTRACT As global decarbonization goals become more urgent, it is vital to understand that decoupling carbon from growth is not a purely mechanical process of adopting green machines; it is a socio‐technical transition. Understanding carbon productivity requires analyzing the synergy between voluntary standards and strict regulation, demonstrating that technology only drives societal change when embedded in a robust institutional framework that prevents mere compliance. Therefore, this cross‐country panel study examines whether the diffusion of Environmental Management System (EMS) ISO 14001 is associated with improvements in total‐factor carbon emission performance in 15 countries with the highest ISO 14001 adoption intensity over 2010–2024, yielding a balanced panel of 210 country‐year observations. Using a two‐stage Malmquist Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) model, we decompose change in carbon performance into two critical vectors: change in efficiency (catch‐up effect) and technological change (frontier shift). The decomposition results indicate that, for most countries, 24% in carbon performance observed gains were more closely associated with efficiency catch‐up than with frontier‐shifting technological change. Meanwhile, Germany shows consistently shifted the carbon‐efficiency frontier during the study period. Moreover, panel regression analysis indicates that ISO 14001 adoption intensity remains conditionally associated with these improvements after controlling for energy intensity and industrial structure. This study contributes to the literature by demonstrating that management systems act as technology absorption mechanisms, enabling lagging nations to reach the frontier of existing best practices. Finally, the findings provide a forward‐looking basis suggesting that, without an acceleration in radical technological innovation (frontier‐shift), current efficiency efforts based on voluntary standards will be insufficient to achieve net‐zero emissions goals.

title: Quince años de monitoreo muestran que Ligustrum lucidum sostiene su dominancia en bosques invadidos
summary: 1. Las especies arbóreas invasoras alteran la composición y la estructura forestal de los ecosistemas que invaden. Antes de implementar medidas de manejo frente a la invasión, es necesario comprender la dinámica de estas especies; esto requ
content: 1. Las especies arbóreas invasoras alteran la composición y la estructura forestal de los ecosistemas que invaden. Antes de implementar medidas de manejo frente a la invasión, es necesario comprender la dinámica de estas especies; esto requiere monitoreos a largo plazo. La mayoría de los estudios sobre la dinámica de bosques dominados por especies exóticas invasoras se basan en muestreos puntuales o en períodos de monitoreo relativamente breves.2. Analizamos durante 15 años la dinámica temporal de la estructura y la demografía de bosques sucesionales dominados por Ligustrum lucidum, especie exótica invasora en el centro y el noroeste de la Argentina. Realizamos cuatro censos (2009, 2014, 2019 y 2024) en parcelas permanentes en bosques de L. lucidum en la Sierra de San Javier (Tucumán, Argentina), con edades de 15, 25, 40 y 60 años. Evaluamos los cambios en la densidad arbórea, la biomasa y las tasas de mortalidad y reclutamiento entre censos, a nivel de parcela y para las cuatro especies más abundantes (L. lucidum, Morus alba, Ocotea porphyria y Myrsine laetevirens).3. La biomasa aumentó en todas las parcelas y la densidad de árboles disminuyó en dos. La mortalidad fue menor y el reclutamiento mayor durante el primer período intercensal (2009-2014). A nivel de especie, M. alba mostró un descenso fuerte por su alta mortalidad. L. lucidum se mantuvo como especie invasora dominante, conservando esa posición por el reclutamiento y el aumento sostenido de su biomasa.4. Implicancias. El reemplazo de L. lucidum por especies nativas durante la sucesión forestal es poco probable a las escalas temporales y espaciales consideradas. El monitoreo a largo plazo mostró que especies arbóreas nativas como M. laetevirens y O. porphyria serían buenas candidatas para restaurar la composición nativa de los bosques invadidos por L. lucidum en las Yungas.

title: Reliable Compressive Strength Prediction of Self-Compacting Concrete with Recycled Coarse Aggregate Using an Interpretable Machine Learning Model (LightGBM) with Uncertainty Quantification
summary: Machine learning is increasingly used to predict the compressive strength of self-compacting concrete with recycled coarse aggregate (SCRCAC), with coefficients of determination of 0.81–0.87 reported in the literature. This paper first show
content: Machine learning is increasingly used to predict the compressive strength of self-compacting concrete with recycled coarse aggregate (SCRCAC), with coefficients of determination of 0.81–0.87 reported in the literature. This paper first shows that the widely used reference dataset of 603 mixtures contains only 504 unique compositions, with 84 groups of identical and 21 contradictory ones, so that identical mixtures leak between the training and test sets. Under an objective, leakage-free evaluation (with the model re-tuned on the deduplicated dataset), the coefficient of determination drops to about 0.73, a correction that applies to all models on this dataset. We then propose an interpretable, hyperparameter-optimized LightGBM model that (i) reaches the level of the best published results under the standard protocol (seed-averaged five-fold cross-validation (CV) R2 = 0.813); (ii) provides a calibrated uncertainty interval for each prediction via split-conformal prediction, achieving an empirical coverage of 0.906 at the 90% nominal level; and (iii) remains fully explainable (SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), partial dependence), with cement as the dominant predictor, followed by water and the mineral admixture. Under a 70/30 protocol averaged over 25 splits, it achieves an R2 = 0.794 ± 0.038 and a root mean squared error (RMSE) = 6.20 ± 0.48 MPa, exceeding all four machine learning models of the reference study. Aspects in which the reference study retains an advantage are also discussed.

title: Sustainability aspects in the digital communication content of Lithuanian sports organisations
summary: Sports can influence societal behaviour and are related to sustainability challenges worldwide; therefore, it is important to investigate how sports organisations promote sustainability. The article aims to investigate the sustainability as
content: Sports can influence societal behaviour and are related to sustainability challenges worldwide; therefore, it is important to investigate how sports organisations promote sustainability. The article aims to investigate the sustainability aspects of the digital communication content of Lithuanian sports organisations, how sustainability values are declared on the official websites of sports organisations, and in what forms sustainability is promoted in the country through sport. Based on a review of scientific literature, the study summarises the features of sustainability in sport and presents the results of the analysis of the digital communication content of Lithuanian sports organisations. Sports organisations actively and increasingly contribute to the formation of economic and social wellness, as well as represent socio-cultural values. As global trends show, the decline in physical activity and increasing environmental problems are negatively affecting the sports sector worldwide, including Lithuania. Therefore, it is necessary to respond and adapt sports organisations’ management and marketing communication solutions to these trends. There is a need to rethink the strategic communication guidelines and forms used by sports organisations to promote sustainability values, as well as to develop sports activities in an inclusive and meaningful way for future generations.

title: Large Language Models and Prompt Engineering
summary: This book provides a structured and accessible introduction to the theory, design, and real-world use of large language models (LLMs). As generative AI systems become embedded across industries, this book offers readers a balanced perspecti
content: This book provides a structured and accessible introduction to the theory, design, and real-world use of large language models (LLMs). As generative AI systems become embedded across industries, this book offers readers a balanced perspective that combines technical foundations with practical guidance and critical reflection. Beginning with the fundamentals of LLMs and prompt engineering, this book progressively explores advanced prompting techniques, application and interaction frameworks, and the underlying architectures that power modern language models. Dedicated chapters examine how LLMs are being applied in high-impact domains such as healthcare, customer support, and education, highlighting design principles, implementation considerations, and illustrative case studies. The book also addresses model fine-tuning, evaluation methods, and the ethical, social, and regulatory challenges associated with deploying LLMs at scale. This book supports readers in: · Understanding prompt engineering strategies and application frameworks · Gaining insight into contemporary LLM architecture and capabilities · Designing and evaluating LLM-based systems across real-world domains · Considering ethics, safety, and human-centered aspects of LLM deployment This book is a practical, accessible resource for those seeking to work thoughtfully and responsibly with LLMs in both academic and applied settings.

title: Integrating data literacy and climate science: creating multidisciplinary, data-driven social media posts in grade 10 on human-induced climate change
summary: Abstract This study reports on a 15-hour multidisciplinary teaching unit that integrates data literacy and climate change education for grade 10 students. Grounded in social-constructivist and civic statistics principles, the unit engages l
content: Abstract This study reports on a 15-hour multidisciplinary teaching unit that integrates data literacy and climate change education for grade 10 students. Grounded in social-constructivist and civic statistics principles, the unit engages learners with real datasets (global temperature, temperature and CO2 data from Vostok ice cores, and Mauna Loa CO2 data) using CODAP for visualization and piecewise trend analysis. Students create Instagram-like posts that are intended to help students integrate different disciplinary learning experiences related to climate change as a formative learning journal to communicate their data-based findings. Two classes produced 131 posts, 35 contained data-based arguments and were analyzed with qualitative content analysis against the scaffolding Statistical Communication Framework for Social Media Posts (SCFSMP). Most data-oriented posts included visualizations and described trends and patterns. Only a few to none addressed the data source, reliability of the data, or limitations of the data. Mathematical reasoning centered on linear trends and slope with some posts offering predictions. Findings indicate that combining real data sets with structured communicative tasks may foster students’ data literacy, climate understanding, and motivation. The Instagram format supported narrative engagement through comment threads. The study contributes a teaching unit, the SCFSMP for data-based social media posts in mathematics education, and evidence that data-centered inquiry can connect scientific understanding of human-induced climate change with civic aims. Positioning climate change as a data problem may help students practice reasoning with evidence and may prepare them to participate in debates.

title: SWOT Analysis for Mangrove Forest Management Policy at Teluk Youtefa Natural Tourism Park, Jayapura, Indonesia
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MULTIDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS
summary: Mangrove forests in Indonesia face significant degradation pressures from anthropogenic activities and climate change. This study aims to formulate an effective management policy for the mangrove ecosystem at Teluk Youtefa Natural Tourism P
content: Mangrove forests in Indonesia face significant degradation pressures from anthropogenic activities and climate change. This study aims to formulate an effective management policy for the mangrove ecosystem at Teluk Youtefa Natural Tourism Park (TWA) in Jayapura, Papua, Indonesia, through a comprehensive SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) analysis. Data were collected through surveys, interviews, and focus group discussions involving local communities, government agencies, academics, and non-governmental organizations. The SWOT matrix was constructed to identify internal and external factors affecting mangrove management and to develop strategic recommendations. The results indicate that the primary strengths include the legal status of TWA Youtefa, high biodiversity potential, and emerging ecotourism opportunities. Key weaknesses encompass land conversion pressures, inadequate supporting infrastructure, and low community awareness. Opportunities arise from global conservation awareness, central government support, and digital monitoring technologies. Major threats include climate change, sea-level rise, industrial pollution, and conflicting spatial planning. Based on the SWOT matrix, four strategic clusters were formulated: (i) Strengths-Opportunities (SO) strategies focusing on community-based ecotourism and education centers; (ii) Strengths-Threats (ST) strategies emphasizing monitoring systems and law enforcement; (iii) Weaknesses-Opportunities (WO) strategies targeting capacity building and infrastructure development; and (iv) Weaknesses-Threats (WT) strategies proposing disaster mitigation and rehabilitation programs. This study provides evidence-based recommendations for policymakers to achieve sustainable mangrove management in Papua.

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Advancing ESG Integration and Sustainable Finance: A Secondary Data Analysis
source: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
summary: The rapid growth of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) investing has exposed limitations in traditional data collection, scoring, and risk assessment methods. This study examines how Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming ESG
content: The rapid growth of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) investing has exposed limitations in traditional data collection, scoring, and risk assessment methods. This study examines how Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming ESG and sustainable finance using secondary data from institutional reports, academic literature, and market databases from 2020- 2025. Through systematic review and thematic analysis of secondary sources including Bloomberg ESG data, MSCI ESG Ratings methodology, World Bank sustainable finance reports, and peer-reviewed articles, this paper identifies key AI applications in ESG data aggregation, greenwashing detection, climate risk modeling, and portfolio optimization. Findings indicate that AI technologies, particularly Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML), improve ESG data coverage by up to 40% and enhance predictive accuracy for climate-related financial risks. However, challenges related to data bias, model transparency, and regulatory fragmentation persist. The paper proposes a conceptual framework for responsible AI adoption in sustainable finance and outlines future research directions.

title: Legal and programme source corpus for consent architectures in land-based carbon projects (Philippines, Vietnam, Laos)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Archival deposit of the public legal and programme instruments underpinning a comparative institutional-legal analysis of who can legally refuse a land-based carbon project in the Philippines, Vietnam, and Laos, and when non-consent alters
content: Archival deposit of the public legal and programme instruments underpinning a comparative institutional-legal analysis of who can legally refuse a land-based carbon project in the Philippines, Vietnam, and Laos, and when non-consent alters the legal outcome. CONTENTS (102 files, five zipped folders) 01_Philippines — Indigenous Peoples' Rights Act (RA 8371), NCIP free, prior and informed consent guidelines, DENR administrative orders on forest-carbon projects, the Environmental Impact Statement system, and Joint Crediting Mechanism programme rules. 02_Vietnam — Decrees 06/2022, 107/2022, 119/2025, 83/2026, 180/2026 and 29/2026; the Forestry, Environmental Protection, Land, and Grassroots Democracy Laws; and the Article 6.2 implementation agreement with its annexes. 03_Laos — Official Gazette texts, including Forestry Law No. 64/NA, Environmental Protection Law No. 53/NA, Prime-Ministerial Decree No. 292/GO on Carbon Credits, MAF Decision No. 4565 on forest carbon management, EIA Decrees No. 21/PMO and No. 389/GOV, and the climate change and ethnic group affairs decrees. 04_Multilateral — UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples; UNFCCC CMA.6 Article 6 decisions; the Article 6.4 sustainable development tool (v01.0 and v01.1); the Article 6.4 appeal and grievance procedure; the FCPF Carbon Fund methodological framework; and GCF funding proposals FP282 and FP294. 06_Comparators — Desk-probe instruments from Kenya (Climate Change Act, Carbon Markets Regulations, Community Land Act) and Cambodia (Land Law, Environment and Natural Resources Code). CHECKSUMS_sha256.csv lists every file with its size and SHA-256 hash, so the corpus can be verified independently. DELIBERATELY NOT INCLUDED Copyrighted standard-body publications (Verra VCS, CCB and JNR; ART TREES; ICVCM; VCMI; Gold Standard) and third-party press reporting are cited and linked — with live URL, Web Archive snapshot, and access date — in the article's source-archive manifest (Supplementary Data S5) rather than redistributed here. Coding data and reproducibility files (Supplementary Data S1 to S5) are submitted as supplementary material with the journal article, not deposited here. No personal data. This deposit contains public official instruments only: no coder records, correspondence, reviewer materials, or practice-note documents. LICENSING NOTE The compilation, folder structure, and checksum manifest are released under CC0. The individual instruments are official government and intergovernmental texts and remain subject to their own terms of use.

title: THE REVENUE GAP OF NON-TAX STATE REVENUE FROM SOCIAL FORESTRY IN LAMPUNG PROVINCE
summary: Optimizing Non-Tax State Revenue (PNBP) from Social Forestry (SF) is important to ensure that community-based forest utilization contributes to state revenue and sustainable forest governance. This study estimated the potential, realization
content: Optimizing Non-Tax State Revenue (PNBP) from Social Forestry (SF) is important to ensure that community-based forest utilization contributes to state revenue and sustainable forest governance. This study estimated the potential, realization, and revenue gap of PNBP from SF activities in Lampung Province using a revenue gap analysis approach. A quantitative descriptive method was applied by integrating planning data from the Social Forestry Management Plan (RKPS), production data from the Forest Product Administration Information System (SIPUHH), and revenue realization data from the Non-Tax State Revenue Information System (SIPNBP). The analysis covered 138 SF groups with verified RKPS documents and recorded PNBP payments in 2025. The estimated potential PNBP reached IDR 3.71 billion, while the recorded realization was IDR 785.11 million, resulting in an estimated revenue gap of IDR 2.92 billion (78.86%). Of the 44 Non-Timber Forest Product (NTFP) commodities planned in the RKPS, only 21 were recorded in the production and payment systems, indicating a substantial discrepancy between planned and recorded activities. The revenue gap was associated with inconsistencies between planning documents and implementation, non-standard production units, limitations in data integration, and indications of under-reporting in the administrative system. These findings highlight the importance of improving planning quality, institutional capacity, data standardization, system integration, and administrative governance to optimize PNBP in SF. Since the analysis relies on administrative records rather than verified field production data, the results should be interpreted as an indicative revenue gap rather than a confirmed state revenue loss.

title: Editorial: Participatory and just governance: empowering local and Indigenous communities
summary: The papers in this Research Topic (RT) extend insights on the roles of social relations, institutional arrangements, Indigenous ways of knowing, local knowledge, and decision-making participation in shaping water governance and practice. De
content: The papers in this Research Topic (RT) extend insights on the roles of social relations, institutional arrangements, Indigenous ways of knowing, local knowledge, and decision-making participation in shaping water governance and practice. Despite efforts to predict flows and possible hazards, we continue to observe "unintended consequences" when humans interact with waterscapes. What we often learn, we argue, is that what appears "unintended" often reflects a deliberate architecture of exclusion; one that becomes legible only when social power relations are placed at the center of analysis alongside hydrological variables. Doing so may illuminate where injustice complicates intentions and what difference participatory and just governance makes.The authors in this RT mix research methods to examine how hydrogeological landscapes and societal power relations coproduce one another. For example, Morales et al. (2025) identify the space between slope and elevation that exists in Peru in which humans take advantage of high-altitude escarpments to obscure mining activities that alter flows and exacerbate downstream risks. Quechua speaking communities invoke Apu Razuhuillca as a territorial guardian and water as a symbol of identity in protest to the extraction that occurs without the legally required consultation. In this way, grassroots resistance to proposed watershed disruptions are not unintended consequences that could not have been predicted, but are logical responses to a system of institutional exclusion and historical dispossession. Saunders et al. (2025) describe how highly organized fishers in Norway asserted their power to intercept decision-making at critical moments that changed institutional outcomes and processes. In this case study, economic growth narratives pushed forward offshore wind energy without consulting fishers. Saunders et al. (2025) juxtapose this case study with small fishers in Brazil who organized bycatch monitoring to reshape environmental policy and challenge stereotypes of fishers as anti-environmentalist. A third case study describes how fishers in South Africa took legal action to expose environmental and social costs of estuarine diamond mining. In all cases, resistance on the part of fishers might be seen as "unintended consequences" if one focuses only on dominant narratives and fails to account for threatened fishing livelihoods, marine ecology impacts, and/or threats to national identity. title: Effects of Heat Treatment Applications on Some Fundamental Properties of Wood
source: Düzce Üniversitesi Bilim ve Teknoloji Dergisi
summary: Wood, a natural material with versatile industrial applications, faces limitations such as low dimensional stability and decay resistance. Significant progress has been made in wood modification research to minimize these problems. Among wo
content: Wood, a natural material with versatile industrial applications, faces limitations such as low dimensional stability and decay resistance. Significant progress has been made in wood modification research to minimize these problems. Among wood modification methods, thermal treatment has emerged as an effective method for the environmentally friendly wood industry. Research has shown that heat-treated wood has superior properties compared to natural wood (dimensional stability, wettability, and biological resistance). Heat-treated lumber is a good choice for various applications, especially those exposed to air and moisture changes on the ground. However, heat treatment performed under atmospheric conditions (without the use of an inert gas) causes degradation in the wood’s cell walls and middle lamella. Thus, the wood material becomes more brittle (fragile) than untreated wood. Thermally treated lumber with low strength properties is not suitable for use in load-bearing sections of wooden structures. Additionally, the color of the wood darkens as the temperature and duration of the thermal treatment increase. The suitability of these applications for various uses was discussed by evaluating both the advantages provided by heat treatment processes and the potential losses in mechanical properties. In this review study, scientific studies published primarily between 2000 and 2025 were evaluated to comparatively examine the effects of thermal treatment applied to wood on its physical, chemical, mechanical, and biological properties; common findings and differences reported in various studies were synthesized to provide a general assessment for specific application areas.

title: A multi-level conceptual system dynamics architecture for examining sustainability and resilience in coupled earth–space systems
summary: Human societies are entering a period of converging pressures and emerging capabilities. Environmental degradation, climate change, urbanization, and resource constraints, together with global risks including technological threats, nuclear
content: Human societies are entering a period of converging pressures and emerging capabilities. Environmental degradation, climate change, urbanization, and resource constraints, together with global risks including technological threats, nuclear conflict, and asteroid impacts, are exposing the vulnerability of a civilization concentrated on a single planet. Concurrently, advances in launch systems, robotics, and space infrastructure are expanding the feasibility of large-scale human activity beyond Earth. Research on Large-Scale Space Migration (LSSM), here defined as a system-level process involving the redistribution of populations, resources, and infrastructure across terrestrial and off-world environments within the solar system, remains fragmented across disciplines. This paper proposes an exploratory, multi-level conceptual system dynamics architecture for examining how large-scale human expansion may reshape the dynamics of an Earth–space socioecological system, including both adaptive and maladaptive trajectories. The framework comprises three interacting levels: (i) a Level I material and infrastructure layer encompassing population dynamics, resource systems, environmental processes, economic activity, space infrastructure, and Earth–space flows; (ii) a Level II governance layer representing institutional structures and trade-offs among liberty, equality, and security; and (iii) a Level III psychological and social layer capturing social adaptation and collective response through aggregate variables such as perceived system security, institutional legitimacy, and social cohesion. The Level I material and infrastructure layer has been developed as an initial system dynamics prototype, providing a methodological foundation for Levels II and III, which are proposed as future extensions. The framework is intended to support scenario analysis, hypothesis generation, and staged model development rather than prediction.

title: Sustainability Policy Uncertainty, Energy Transition, and Carbon Intensity: Implications for <scp>SDG</scp> 7 and <scp>SDG</scp> 13
summary: ABSTRACT This study investigates how Environmental, Social, and Governance Uncertainty (ESGU) relates to carbon intensity across 24 economies observed annually from 2003 to 2024, a question situated at the intersection of Sustainable Develo
content: ABSTRACT This study investigates how Environmental, Social, and Governance Uncertainty (ESGU) relates to carbon intensity across 24 economies observed annually from 2003 to 2024, a question situated at the intersection of Sustainable Development Goals 7 and 13. ESG‐related uncertainty has been studied mainly in financial markets, yet whether it shapes aggregate decarbonization outcomes and through which channel has remained largely unexamined. The empirical design combines two‐way fixed‐effects regressions with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors, a formal mediation test based on Sobel statistics and bias‐corrected bootstrap intervals, and a cross‐sectionally augmented ARDL specification that separates long‐run from short‐run dynamics. Carbon intensity, the renewable electricity share, and the ESGU index are compiled from openly accessible databases, and every series is documented at source to support replication. The estimates indicate that sustainability policy uncertainty is associated with carbon intensity primarily through the energy‐transition channel rather than through a direct effect. Higher ESGU coincides with a larger renewable electricity share ( a = 0.188, p < 0.10), and a larger renewable share is in turn associated with lower carbon intensity ( b = −0.168, p < 0.01); the resulting indirect path is statistically robust (Sobel z = −3.46, p = 0.001; bootstrap 95% CI [−0.048, −0.016]) and accounts for roughly 47% of the total association. Renewable capacity does not significantly moderate the relationship, whereas trade openness does, and the direction of these conditioning effects departs from prior expectations grounded in firm‐level evidence. By moving ESGU analysis from financial markets to economy‐wide decarbonization and by isolating renewable electricity as the operative transmission mechanism, the study reframes regulatory predictability and clean‐energy deployment as complementary rather than competing instruments for SDG 7 and SDG 13.

title: Digital literacy and farmers’ uptake of socialized services: a U-shaped relationship-CRRS based data validation
summary: Introduction Socialized services can facilitate the organic integration of smallholder farmers with modern agriculture, playing a significant role in accelerating the advancement of Chinese-style agricultural modernization and building Chin
content: Introduction Socialized services can facilitate the organic integration of smallholder farmers with modern agriculture, playing a significant role in accelerating the advancement of Chinese-style agricultural modernization and building China into a leading agricultural nation. Methods This study uses the 2020 Chinese Academy of Social Sciences rural revitalization research data, applies factor analysis and principal component analysis to measure the digital literacy level of farmers, and after clarifying the internal logic of digital literacy affecting the service scale operation of farmers, applies a linear regression model, mediation effect model, and other methods to explore the specific impact of the digital literacy level of farmers on the service scale operation of farmers and further verify the intrinsic mechanism between the two. Results The results of the benchmark regression show that the impact of farmers’ digital literacy level on service scale operation shows a nonlinear U-shaped relationship that shrinks first and then expands, and the U-shaped relationship still holds after the robustness test and endogeneity test. The results of the mechanism test show that the improvement of farmers’ digital literacy level promotes the development of agricultural service scale operation by promoting the fourfold mechanism of farmers’ natural capital accumulation, social capital accumulation, financial capital accumulation, and human capital accumulation. title: A hybrid CNN-BiLSTM model integrating meteorological and topographic factors for transmission line ice thickness prediction
summary: Transmission-line icing can threaten reliable grid operation, making short-term ice-thickness prediction important for disaster prevention and operational planning. This study develops a late-fusion CNN-BiLSTM regression framework for next-
content: Transmission-line icing can threaten reliable grid operation, making short-term ice-thickness prediction important for disaster prevention and operational planning. This study develops a late-fusion CNN-BiLSTM regression framework for next-hour ice-thickness prediction on the 500 kV Changmiao 5P01 transmission-line corridor in Huzhou, Zhejiang, China. A 24-h historical meteorological sequence is processed by 1D convolutional layers and a BiLSTM without using observations after the prediction boundary; location-specific static topographic descriptors are concatenated only with the resulting boundary representation before linear regression. The study uses 2,348 continuous hourly records. Inputs include temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, precipitation, and wind components, together with elevation, slope, and aspect; ice thickness is measured in millimeters. Under the same chronological train/test protocol, the proposed configuration produced lower test errors than the selected standalone CNN, LSTM, and BiLSTM baseline configurations. The results support the predictive usefulness of the terrain descriptors for the studied subtropical hilly corridor, but do not establish causal effects or broader geographic generalization.

title: Quantitative evaluation of coloration and functionalization efficiency for surface modification of regenerated cellulose fabrics
summary: Globally, the ever-growing demand for sustainable, functionalized cellulosic textile fabrics has increased, steering interest towards a new generation of eco-friendly regenerated cellulosic fibers. In this study, sustainable dyed and multi-
