title: Washed Mixed Recycled Coarse Aggregates as Natural Aggregate Replacement in Concrete for Seawall Blocks
summary: Construction and demolition waste remains a major sustainability challenge, while the use of mixed recycled aggregates in structural concrete is still limited due to concerns over variability, water absorption, and durability. This study in
content: Construction and demolition waste remains a major sustainability challenge, while the use of mixed recycled aggregates in structural concrete is still limited due to concerns over variability, water absorption, and durability. This study investigates whether washed mixed recycled coarse aggregate can partially or fully replace natural coarse aggregate in concrete for seawall block applications. The recycled aggregate was characterized and then upgraded through simple washing and grading to remove fines and contaminants. Concrete mixes incorporating 0%, 5%, 1780, 20%, 50%, and 100% recycled aggregate replacement were produced and tested for workability, compressive strength, flexural strength, density, and water absorption under both tap-water and saline curing conditions. The results demonstrate that washing significantly improves aggregate quality, enabling compressive strength comparable to the reference mix at replacement levels up to approximately 20%. Higher replacement levels led to reductions in workability, flexural strength, and density; however, performance remained within technically acceptable limits. Overall, the findings indicate that washed mixed recycled coarse aggregate is a viable material for seawall concrete, supporting more circular and sustainable use of construction and demolition waste in marine infrastructure.

title: Afet Hazırlığında Stratejik Adım: Tunceli Merkez İlçesi Toplanma Alanlarının AHP ile Analizi
summary: Tunceli ili, yaşam koşullarının zorluğu ile dikkat çeken bir bölgedir. Sert iklim koşulları ve engebeli arazi yapısı, ilde çeşitli doğal afetlerin sıkça yaşanmasına neden olmaktadır. Araştırma kapsamında toplanma alanlarının değerlendirilme
content: Tunceli ili, yaşam koşullarının zorluğu ile dikkat çeken bir bölgedir. Sert iklim koşulları ve engebeli arazi yapısı, ilde çeşitli doğal afetlerin sıkça yaşanmasına neden olmaktadır. Araştırma kapsamında toplanma alanlarının değerlendirilmesinde Çok Kriterli Karar Verme (ÇKKV) yaklaşımlarından biri olan Analitik Hiyerarşi Süreci (AHP) yöntemi tercih edilmiştir. Çalışmada kriterlere bağlı ana kriter ve alt kriterler arasında yapılan analiz sonucunda şu sonuçlara ulaşılmıştır: “toplanma alan güvenliği”, ana kriterler arasında önem düzeyi en yüksek ağırlığa (0,707) sahip olan ana kriter olmuştur. Ana kriterlere ait alt kriterlerin analiz sonuçları neticesinde; “Toplanma alan özelliği” ana kriteri altında bulunan alt kriterleri arasında önem düzeyi en yüksek ağırlığa sahip olan kriter 0,559 “erişim ve tahliye kolaylığı” olmuştur. “Toplanma alanına erişim” ana kriteri altında bulunan alt kriterler arasında önem düzeyi en yüksek ağırlığa sahip olan kriter 0,550 “tabela, kroki ve işaretleme ile konum belirlenmesi” alt kriteri olmuştur. Toplanma alan güvenliği kriteri altında bulunan alt kriterler arasında önem düzeyi en yüksek ağırlığa sahip olan alt kriter 0,458 “temel ihtiyaçlara yakınlık” olmuştur. Yapılan analizler genel olarak değerlendirildiğinde, “toplanma alanı güvenliği” ana kriterinin en yüksek ağırlığa sahip unsur olduğu görülmüştür. Bu bulgular, Tunceli ili Merkez ilçesindeki afet ve acil durum toplanma alanlarının değerlendirilmesinde AHP yönteminin tutarlı ve güvenilir sonuçlar verdiğini ortaya koymaktadır.

title: Eco-communities as socio-spatial laboratories: Lessons for retrofitting low-density housing settlements
source: Journal of Housing and the Built Environment
summary: Abstract Eco-villages have emerged as laboratories of alternative socio-spatial organisation, generating practices that may inform the retrofitting of mainstream low-density housing settlements. This paper examines how principles developed
content: Abstract Eco-villages have emerged as laboratories of alternative socio-spatial organisation, generating practices that may inform the retrofitting of mainstream low-density housing settlements. This paper examines how principles developed in Danish eco-villages can be translated into settlements that share comparable spatial typologies, such as suburban areas, peri-urban districts, and small towns characterised by dispersed morphology and limited shared infrastructure, but differ in their underlying socio-spatial conditions. Based on fieldwork in three communities—Andelssamfundet i Hjortshøj, Karise Permatopia, and Svanholm—the study draws on semi-structured interviews, spatial observations, and GIS-based geo-surveys. Using an analytical framework focused on community, built environment, and ecology, it identifies strategies linking collective agency with everyday resource stewardship. While the three cases share sustainability-oriented values, they differ in governance and socio-ecological organisation: Hjortshøj emphasises informal collaboration, Permatopia integrates family-oriented permaculture routines, and Svanholm represents structured collectivism and agricultural production. The paper argues that retrofitting requires translation rather than replication. Because social organisation and spatial form are mutually constitutive, selective adaptation must extend beyond spatial typologies to the governance routines and participation infrastructures that sustain collective life. Such translation is enabled by sustained institutional support and shared spatial resources, but is constrained by self-selection dynamics, unequal access, and volunteer dependency.

title: Effects of roughness geometry on heat transfer, fluid flow and thermo-hydraulic performance of solar air heaters: A comprehensive review
summary: In the present review article, an effort has been made to review various experimental and numerical research, which include heat transfer rate and fluid flow characteristics of a modified solar air heater (SAH) using various artificial roug
content: In the present review article, an effort has been made to review various experimental and numerical research, which include heat transfer rate and fluid flow characteristics of a modified solar air heater (SAH) using various artificial roughness. As it is clear that artificial roughness enhances the heat transfer and performance, in this review study, various types of roughened SAH performances have been examined. These various roughness patterns are V-shape, W-rib, arc shape, spherical ball and S-type, and their placement arrangements, like transverse, inclined and longitudinal, are discussed in this article. The comparative studies of thermo-hydraulic performance with heat transfer and fluid flow investigations of various roughened SAHs have been described to identify optimal performance parameters to select the optimum configuration that can be further used for various applications. In addition to this, various correlations of the Nusselt number and friction factor developed by various investigators have also been reported. The main aim of this study is to evaluate the SAH performance using various roughness patterns. It also provides several essential recommendations for effectively designing and implementing SAHs. This review encompasses a comprehensive analysis of 178 research articles published between 1988 and 2024, focusing on advancements in the field. The findings showcase the peak values for the Nusselt number as 7.61, the friction factor reaching 6.48 times that of a smooth duct for discrete multiple-arc ribs, and the maximum thermal-hydraulic performance reported at 4.73 for dimple or protrusion ribs.

title: Cradle to Cradle
summary: Cradle to Cradle™ (C2C) is a biomimetic approach to the design of products and systems whereby materials circulating in the economy are equated to nutrients feeding natural ecosystems. The concept is akin to that of the circular economy in
content: Cradle to Cradle™ (C2C) is a biomimetic approach to the design of products and systems whereby materials circulating in the economy are equated to nutrients feeding natural ecosystems. The concept is akin to that of the circular economy in that it promotes the elimination of waste and the establishment of continuous recycling loops. C2C is based on three principles: Waste Equals Food, Use Current Solar Income, and Celebrate Diversity. Cradle to Cradle™ is a registered trademark, and the C2C Product Innovation Institute has the licence to certify C2C products. The concept has some notable limitations, including that the environmental performance of C2C products is not assured – rather it is argued it should always be assessed via a holistic approach like Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). The similarities and differences between C2C and LCA are discussed, including the difference between eco-effectiveness and eco-efficiency.

title: Life cycle costing and social impact assessment of electric vehicle use: the case of Washington, DC
summary: Introduction Battery-Electric Vehicles (BEVs) are considered important in advancing urban decarbonization efforts, but their operating costs vary substantially depending on factors such as charging infrastructure, building density, traffic
content: Introduction Battery-Electric Vehicles (BEVs) are considered important in advancing urban decarbonization efforts, but their operating costs vary substantially depending on factors such as charging infrastructure, building density, traffic patterns, and electricity prices. This creates unequal burdens for households with different socio-economic characteristics. This article combines a tariff-adjusted life-cycle costing approach with a social life-cycle approach to evaluate the performance of light-duty BEVs in Washington, DC, on a per-vehicle mile basis. The analysis uses disaggregated data for the eight Wards of Washington, DC, to characterize the range of social impacts associated with the city's marked disparities. Methods According to registration data from December 2025, 68 percent of the city's 11,727 BEVs are concentrated in higher-income Wards with a higher concentration of single-family homes. These Wards (Wards 3 through 6) comprise roughly 50 percent of the city's population. By comparison, the city's lower-income Wards with a higher concentration of multi-family renter-dominated properties (Wards 7 and 8) comprise approximately 25 percent of the city's population but account for only 12 percent of its BEVs. The city's charging infrastructure includes 1,062 Level 2 ports across 310 sites, but only 58 fast charging ports at 10 locations. Concerns about affordability, charging duration, and access intensify the disparities in access to BEV infrastructure across the city's eight Wards. We model several scenarios by Ward to assess the disparities in access. Results Private Level 2 charging costs 0.145−0.147 per mile compared to 0.252 for public DC fast charging in our low mileage scenario. These disparities persist for our higher-mileage scenarios. Discussion Strategies to alleviate these disparities in charging costs include changes in rate structures, submetering provisions, and make-ready requirements. These strategies would obligate utilities or developers to install the appropriate electrical panels, conduits, and wiring needed so that BEV chargers can be added at lower cost especially in neighborhoods that depend more on public charging options.

title: Utilitarianism and Weak Sustainability : A Corpus Analysis of the Representation of the Sea by the UK Government (2010-2023)
summary: This article explores how the sea is represented in the UK government’s communications by applying corpus linguistic analysis to textual data. The findings reveal a dominant discourse that frames the sea primarily as an economic asset, emph
content: This article explores how the sea is represented in the UK government’s communications by applying corpus linguistic analysis to textual data. The findings reveal a dominant discourse that frames the sea primarily as an economic asset, emphasizing investment and sustainable exploitation understood as resource preservation. Emotional and social dimensions of sustainability are noticeably underrepresented, while narratives surrounding the sea are shaped by managerial, territorial, and threat-based framings. This utilitarian portrayal hinders the development of ocean citizenship, which requires a deeper, emotional connection with the sea. By identifying these narrative imbalances, the article contributes to scholarly discussions on ‘sea blindness’ and ocean citizenship by showing how such a discourse may obscure the sea’s social and environmental significance, limiting public engagement and stewardship. The article argues for a rebalancing of these narratives to include more emotionally resonant and hopeful communication strategies that highlight the intrinsic value of the marine environment beyond its economic value. Key recommendations include shifting from technical to affective language, promoting positive imagery of ocean protection, and favouring the term ‘ocean’ over ‘sea’ to evoke a global sense of stewardship and belonging.

title: Role of Microbiome Manipulation in Enhancing Ruminant Digestion and Productivity: A Review
summary: The rumen microbiome is a diverse and dynamic consortium of bacteria, archaea, protozoa, fungi, and viruses that supports feed degradation, nutrient transformation, animal health, and productive performance in ruminants. Advances in microbi
content: The rumen microbiome is a diverse and dynamic consortium of bacteria, archaea, protozoa, fungi, and viruses that supports feed degradation, nutrient transformation, animal health, and productive performance in ruminants. Advances in microbial ecology, sequencing technologies, and systems biology have created opportunities to manage this microbial ecosystem to improve the efficiency and sustainability of livestock production. This review examines the composition, functions, and ecological interactions of the rumen microbiome, with emphasis on its contribution to fibre digestion, volatile fatty acid production, microbial protein synthesis, feed conversion efficiency, methane formation, and host physiological functions. Current strategies for microbiome modulation, including dietary modification, probiotics, direct-fed microbials, prebiotics, synbiotics, phytogenic compounds, exogenous enzymes, and rumen microbial transplantation, are evaluated in relation to digestive efficiency and animal performance. Emerging approaches, including metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, metabolomics, precision nutrition, synthetic microbial communities, genome-editing tools, and artificial intelligence-based predictive models, are also considered as developing pathways for targeted microbiome engineering. These approaches may support improved nutrient utilisation, milk and meat production, animal health, and mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions from ruminant systems. However, practical implementation remains constrained by microbial ecosystem complexity, inter-animal variability, limited persistence of introduced microorganisms, economic considerations, and regulatory challenges. The review highlights the need to integrate multi-omics datasets, computational modelling, and precision livestock technologies to develop robust, scalable, and economically viable microbiome management strategies. A deeper understanding of host-microbiome interactions and microbial functional dynamics remains essential for translating scientific advances into practical approaches that support sustainable livestock production, environmental stewardship, and overall global food security.

title: Explainable AI for economic performance prediction evidence from industrial production, institutional quality, and consumer demand
summary: Abstract The GWO-XGBoost model achieved an R² of 0.991 in Gross Domestic Product (GDP) prediction, exceeding all other machine learning models compared in this study. Thus, GWO-XGBoost provides a transparent and reliable decision-making sup
content: Abstract The GWO-XGBoost model achieved an R² of 0.991 in Gross Domestic Product (GDP) prediction, exceeding all other machine learning models compared in this study. Thus, GWO-XGBoost provides a transparent and reliable decision-making support system for all those who develop economic policies. Developing accurate macroeconomic predictions can assist in the advancement of sustainable development. However, the non-linear relationships among many macroeconomic variables, such as industrial production, governance, and demand, make it difficult to develop accurate and understandable predictions using conventional macroeconomic models. To address the limitations of these traditional models, we propose a hybrid explanatory model, GWO-XGBoost, that integrates the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) with Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). This integrated model automatically tunes its hyperparameters. Monthly US data from 1996 to 2020 was utilized in the experiment. These data include: Government Effectiveness, Consumer Demand/Retail Sales, Industrial Production, Trade Balance, and Unemployment. The results of the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis show that the two most significant factors influencing economic performance were consumer demand and government effectiveness. As a result of being both highly predictive and having clear feature attributions, the proposed hybrid explanatory model will be useful for all institutions involved in developing and implementing evidence-based planning processes that align with economic growth.

title: Impact of climate change on the epidemiology of plant diseases
summary: Climate change is increasingly recognized as a major driver of plant disease dynamics worldwide, altering environmental conditions that govern host–pathogen–environment interactions. This study aimed to synthesize current scientific evidenc
content: Climate change is increasingly recognized as a major driver of plant disease dynamics worldwide, altering environmental conditions that govern host–pathogen–environment interactions. This study aimed to synthesize current scientific evidence on the impacts of climate change on the epidemiology of plant diseases through an integrative literature review. A systematic search was conducted between March and April 2026 using the Web of Science, Scopus, SciELO, PubMed/MEDLINE, and CAPES Journal Portal databases. Peer-reviewed articles published between 2016 and 2026 in English or Portuguese were screened according to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, resulting in the selection of 17 studies for qualitative analysis. The findings demonstrated that climatic factors, particularly temperature, atmospheric CO2 concentration, relative humidity, precipitation patterns, and leaf wetness duration, significantly influence pathogen survival, reproduction, dispersal, infection efficiency, and disease severity. Temperature emerged as the most influential variable; however, its effects varied substantially among pathosystems, reflecting differences in pathogen biology and host responses. The reviewed studies also indicated that climate change is facilitating the emergence and geographic expansion of plant pathogens into previously unsuitable regions, thereby increasing phytosanitary risks for economically important crops. Furthermore, altered climatic conditions may compromise the effectiveness of conventional disease management strategies, highlighting the need for adaptive approaches. The evidence underscores the importance of integrating epidemiological surveillance, predictive modeling, climate-informed risk assessment, host resistance breeding, and integrated disease management into agricultural adaptation frameworks. Future research should prioritize multidisciplinary approaches to improve the prediction and mitigation of climate-driven disease outbreaks under diverse agroecological conditions.

title: Coping with climate change-related risks in rural Zimbabwe: Evidence from Bikita District
source: International Journal of Research in Business and Social Science (2147-4478)
summary: Climate change poses significant risks to rural livelihoods in semi-arid regions such as Bikita District, Zimbabwe, where recurrent droughts, erratic rainfall, rising temperatures, and water scarcity undermine food security and socio-econom
content: Climate change poses significant risks to rural livelihoods in semi-arid regions such as Bikita District, Zimbabwe, where recurrent droughts, erratic rainfall, rising temperatures, and water scarcity undermine food security and socio-economic stability. This study examines the climate-related risks faced by rural households, identifies the coping and adaptation strategies they employ, and assesses the effectiveness and sustainability of these responses. A qualitative case study design, guided by the Sustainable Livelihoods Framework, was adopted. Data were collected through in-depth interviews (n = 30), focus group discussions (two groups), and direct observations involving households, traditional leaders, and local stakeholders. Thematic analysis was used to identify patterns in risks, coping strategies, and institutional constraints. The findings show that households employ diverse strategies, including crop diversification, cultivation of drought-resistant small grains, water harvesting, livestock downsizing, livelihood diversification, horticulture, and reliance on social networks. However, many of these responses remain short-term coping mechanisms rather than sustainable adaptation strategies. Structural barriers, including limited access to credit, weak extension services, poor infrastructure, and inadequate market systems, constrain their effectiveness. In addition, some practices, including deforestation and over-reliance on food aid, are maladaptive, providing immediate relief while undermining long-term resilience. The study concludes that although rural households demonstrate significant adaptive capacity, their transition from short-term coping to sustainable adaptation is limited by systemic and institutional constraints. It highlights the need for integrated policy interventions that strengthen livelihood assets, enhance institutional support, improve access to finance and markets, and integrate indigenous knowledge with climate-smart practices. These findings contribute to climate adaptation scholarship and provide policy-relevant insights for building long-term resilience in rural Zimbabwe.

title: Cost-effective abatement of industrial sources of nitrous oxide with methane for urgent climate mitigation
summary: Abatement of industrial emissions of nitrous oxide (N2O), a potent greenhouse gas and stratospheric ozone-depleting substance, offers a viable approach to urgent climate mitigation. However, existing N2O abatement processes require rigorous
content: Abatement of industrial emissions of nitrous oxide (N2O), a potent greenhouse gas and stratospheric ozone-depleting substance, offers a viable approach to urgent climate mitigation. However, existing N2O abatement processes require rigorous conditions ( > 400 °C) due to its inertia and high costs. Here we present a cost-effective technology enabling 99.99% N2O conversion at 150 °C and a high reaction rate of 9629.55 kgN2O kgPt−1 h−1 using CH4 as a reductant on Pt/HZSM-5. Mechanism studies reveal the key to this success lies in the reaction-induced Pt nanoparticles, which host monoatomic adsorbed oxygen species and achieve a rapid O* formation/consumption cycle. Techno-economic analysis shows that it offers the potential to reduce N2O abatement costs by 62.3% for industrial adipic acid emissions in China. The study can incentivize further technical development and improve the sustainability of N2O abatement, as well as low-temperature CH4 activation. Cutting industrial nitrous oxide emissions is vital for climate and ozone protection, but current methods need high temperatures. A platinum catalyst converts 99.99% at 150 °C using methane and could cut treatment costs by 62%.

title: Plastic pollution shapes ecosystem response to a storm event in intertidal sediments
summary: Plastic pollution is an emerging driver of ecological change in coastal sediments, yet real-world ecosystem responses remain poorly understood. During a two-month in situ experiment on an intertidal sandflat in Mahurangi Harbour, New Zealan
content: Plastic pollution is an emerging driver of ecological change in coastal sediments, yet real-world ecosystem responses remain poorly understood. During a two-month in situ experiment on an intertidal sandflat in Mahurangi Harbour, New Zealand, a storm event provided a unique opportunity to test whether plastics modulate ecosystem responses to short-term environmental change. We measured sediment oxygen consumption (SOC), nutrient and N₂ fluxes, pore-water nutrient pools, and sediment organic matter in control and plastic-polluted plots across six time points spanning pre- and post-storm conditions. Plastic pollution was realised through vertical insertion of polyester nettings (6 × 2 cm, 10 µm thick, microplastic) into the sediment. Multivariate analyses revealed an interaction effect between treatment and sampling time indicating that the plastic-polluted sediments reacted differently to the storm. In control plots, the storm reduced SOC (− 24%) and pore-water NH₄⁺ (− 53%), and increased NH₄⁺ efflux (+ 186%) and NOₓ − pools (+ 166%). Compared to the storm response in the controls, the storm impact on plastic plots caused a 43% increase in SOC and a 53% increase in NH₄⁺ efflux, and lower pore-water NOₓ − (− 63%). These results demonstrate that plastics can modulate benthic ecosystem responses to storms, potentially altering nitrogen source–sink dynamics. As both plastic pollution and storm frequency intensify, such interaction effects may have growing consequences for coastal ecosystem functioning.

title: The effect of economic globalisation on income inequality in Botswana
source: International Journal of Research in Business and Social Science (2147-4478)
summary: This paper analyses the impact of economic globalisation on income inequality in Botswana, emphasising both direct and indirect transmission mechanisms. The study utilises annual time-series data from 1990 to 2023, employing the Autoregress
content: This paper analyses the impact of economic globalisation on income inequality in Botswana, emphasising both direct and indirect transmission mechanisms. The study utilises annual time-series data from 1990 to 2023, employing the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model and the Toda–Yamamoto Distributed Lag (TYDL) Granger causality method to examine the interrelations among economic globalisation, trade openness, inflation, economic growth, and income inequality. The results indicate a consistent long-term link among the variables, wherein economic globalisation diminishes income disparity, whilst broader globalisation and trade openness likely to intensify it. The causation findings indicate that both economic globalisation and globalisation directly impact income disparity, while globalisation also indirectly influences inequality via inflation. Real GDP per capita indirectly affects inequality via globalisation, while exports directly contribute to inequality. The study indicates that while economic globalisation fosters economic growth and integration, its advantages are inequitably allocated. It advocates for inclusive economic globalisation policies, targeted fiscal redistribution, financial inclusion, and export diversification to guarantee equitable and sustainable growth in Botswana.

title: Rola Szanghajskiej Organizacji Współpracy w kształtowaniu bezpieczeństwa państw Azji Centralnej
summary: This article aims to present key security issues for Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan, which are implemented within the framework of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). An analysis of the member states’ cooperatio
content: This article aims to present key security issues for Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan, which are implemented within the framework of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). An analysis of the member states’ cooperation activities was carried out. Also, an analysis of the collected materials in the form of newspaper articles and literature on the subject made it possible to capture the most important areas of cooperation for Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan. While these countries are facing similar problems in terms of security, one difference is the classification in terms of priority. The main research methods used in the creation of the article included synthesis through causal association, analogy, induction, and deduction.

title: Effect of a narrative and behavioral science intervention on climate mitigation willingness among young professionals in India: A pilot randomized controlled trial
summary: <ns5:p>Background India is highly vulnerable to climate change, yet translating awareness into personal action remains a persistent challenge. While narrative persuasion is a promising tool for behavioural shift, its efficacy in non-Western
content: <ns5:p>Background India is highly vulnerable to climate change, yet translating awareness into personal action remains a persistent challenge. While narrative persuasion is a promising tool for behavioural shift, its efficacy in non-Western, high-awareness cohorts remains largely unexplored. This study, the first randomized controlled trial of its kind in India evaluates whether an interactive climate narrative can increase mitigation willingness among young working professionals. Methods Working professionals in Delhi-NCR (N = 80) were randomized to either a gamified, climate-narrative intervention (n = 40) or an information-only control (n = 40). Personal Climate Mitigation Activities (PCMA) were assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and one-month follow-up. Linear mixed-effects models were employed to control for baseline imbalances. Results Despite high narrative engagement (“transportation”) in the intervention group, mixed-effects modelling revealed no significant group*time interaction for PCMA (P = 0.362). Crucially, a strong “ceiling effect” was identified, with participants displaying near-maximum willingness to adopt mitigation behaviours even at baseline. Narrative transportation did not correlate with immediate or sustained behavioural shifts (r = −0.05, P = 0.757). Conclusion This trial reveals a critical “value-action gap” among educated urban Indian professionals. Because baseline willingness is already exceptionally high, narrative-driven persuasion alone is insufficient to spur action. These findings pivot the climate communication paradigm, suggesting that future efforts must shift from trying to persuade an already willing audience to dismantling structural barriers and implementing environmental nudges that facilitate real-world behaviour change.</ns5:p>

title: Advances in Drift Mitigation and Integrated Precision Spraying Technologies
summary: Agricultural spraying has evolved from conventional passive drift mitigation toward active, intelligent precision management. This review synthesizes advancements in agricultural precision spraying, evaluating both established passive drift
content: Agricultural spraying has evolved from conventional passive drift mitigation toward active, intelligent precision management. This review synthesizes advancements in agricultural precision spraying, evaluating both established passive drift-reduction techniques and emerging active application systems. The analysis emphasizes three core technological pillars: multi-sensor target perception, real-time variable-rate decision modeling, and high-frequency actuation mechanisms. The findings indicate that integrating these distinct mechanisms into a unified “perception–decision–execution” architecture offers a means of balancing the trade-off between drift reduction and canopy coverage. By transitioning from broadcast applications to targeted delivery, this synergistic approach may contribute to improving pesticide utilization, minimizing off-target environmental contamination, and enhancing the biological efficacy of crop protection. Overall, this technical progression may facilitate the translation of precision spraying technologies from controlled laboratory validation to broader field implementation.

title: Calcium Lactate Amendment Improves Saline Soil Properties and Enhances Pepper Resistance Under Short-Term Waterlogging Conditions
summary: Saline soils subjected to short-term waterlogging are a constraint on the sustainable production of protected vegetables, triggering soil structural degradation, salt accumulation, and oxidative damage in plants, which seriously damages cro
content: Saline soils subjected to short-term waterlogging are a constraint on the sustainable production of protected vegetables, triggering soil structural degradation, salt accumulation, and oxidative damage in plants, which seriously damages crop yield and quality. Calcium-based amendments have attracted considerable attention for improving soil conditions and enhancing plant stress tolerance. However, the effects of calcium lactate amendment on saline soil improvement and pepper physiological responses under short-term waterlogging conditions remain insufficiently understood. Different application rates of calcium lactate were applied to saline pepper croplands under waterlogged conditions. The effects on soil physicochemical properties, nutrient availability, plant antioxidant physiology, fruit yield, and quality were analyzed. Calcium lactate improved the physicochemical properties of waterlogged soil and increased the available nutrients in the soil, with the content of available phosphorus and available potassium increasing by 565–855% and 1.60–35.54%, respectively. It enhanced the activities of superoxide dismutase, peroxidase, and catalase, reduced malondialdehyde accumulation (up to 39% compared with CK), and increased proline content (up to 54.62% compared with CK), thereby promoting plant physiological adaptation under short-term waterlogging conditions and improving pepper yield and fruit quality. Higher doses of calcium lactate exhibit better ameliorative effects. Correlation analysis and partial least squares path modeling suggested that calcium lactate application was associated with improved pepper yield and quality through pathways related to soil improvement and plant physiological regulation. This study provides insights into the potential application of calcium lactate for saline soil improvement and sustainable pepper production under short-term waterlogging conditions.

title: Ozone depletion potential
summary: The ozone molecules in Earth's stratosphere protect life on Earth by absorbing ultraviolet light. However, inert chemicals such as chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), other halocarbons, and nitrous oxides destroy ozone in catalytic reactions when r
content: The ozone molecules in Earth's stratosphere protect life on Earth by absorbing ultraviolet light. However, inert chemicals such as chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), other halocarbons, and nitrous oxides destroy ozone in catalytic reactions when reaching the stratosphere. This dramatic environmental problem was recognized internationally as a direct consequence of anthropogenic activities after the discovery of the Antarctic “ozone hole” in 1985. As a response, the UN signed the Montreal Protocol in 1987, mandating the phase-out of many ozone-depleting substances (ODS). Despite treaty violations, uncertainties in emission trends since the mid-2010s, and rising N2O emissions, the Montreal Protocol can be considered a success story of international cooperation and scientific rigor. This entry summarizes how ozone depletion is integrated into common LCIA methods, to which product families LCA researchers should pay close attention, how ozone depletion compares with climate change and other impacts, and where trade-offs between climate change mitigation and ozone layer protection exist.

title: Midpoint impact categories
summary: The Life Cycle Impact Assessment (LCIA) phase plays a critical role in evaluating environmental impacts associated with various processes and products. This phase is centered on the classification and characterization of emissions, which ar
content: The Life Cycle Impact Assessment (LCIA) phase plays a critical role in evaluating environmental impacts associated with various processes and products. This phase is centered on the classification and characterization of emissions, which are systematically grouped into predefined impact categories. The process begins with classification, where emissions are categorized based on their specific environmental effects, such as “Global Warming Potential” and “Acidification Potential”. Following this initial step, characterization quantifies the impact of each emission in relation to a reference substance. Midpoints, such as global warming potential or human toxicity, provide a structured framework for assessing potential environmental changes; however, it is important to note that they do not measure final damage directly. This intermediate step is crucial for comprehensively understanding and comparing the contributions of different emissions to pressing environmental issues, ultimately guiding informed decision-making and fostering sustainability improvements across various sectors.

title: Current progress in oxygen capture via elimination or separation: A review
summary: Oxygen serves as both a vital industrial resource and a detrimental impurity causing corrosion, catalyst poisoning, and product degradation. This review critically evaluates current technologies for oxygen capture, separation, and eliminati
content: Oxygen serves as both a vital industrial resource and a detrimental impurity causing corrosion, catalyst poisoning, and product degradation. This review critically evaluates current technologies for oxygen capture, separation, and elimination across operational scales, distinguishing between reversible separation for production and irreversible elimination for purification. Small-scale strategies (100 m3/h) include solid getters, ceramic oxygen transport membranes, and active food scavengers, while large-scale processes (100 m3/h) encompass catalytic combustion, solid sorbents, membrane separation, pressure swing adsorption (PSA), and cryogenic distillation. Each technology is benchmarked against purity thresholds, energy consumption, scalability, and economic feasibility. Persistent challenges include material degradation under harsh conditions, insufficient long-term stability validation, and fragmented performance reporting. Future research must prioritize hybrid separation architectures, advanced porous materials, standardized testing protocols, and lifecycle assessments. This review provides a decision-oriented framework to guide the development of next-generation, sustainable oxygen management systems for industrial, medical, and environmental applications.

title: Dendroecological studies of trees outside forests (TOF) – A systematic review
summary: Dendroecology offers insights into plant species responses to abrupt and long-term shifts in environmental conditions, but studies are predominantly focused on trees in forest ecosystems. This systematic literature review examines the preva
content: Dendroecology offers insights into plant species responses to abrupt and long-term shifts in environmental conditions, but studies are predominantly focused on trees in forest ecosystems. This systematic literature review examines the prevalence and patterns of dendroecological studies conducted outside forest habitats. Utilizing the PRISMA framework, we systematically searched the Web of Science and identified 59 relevant publications encompassing 217 sampling sites across 26 countries. The studies showed a strong geographic bias towards temperate and cold regions, primarily in the Northern Hemisphere, and a scarce research cover from arid regions, where TOFs are highly present. We found a focus on urban and agricultural settings, and a predominant emphasis on Pinaceae, revealing a lack of knowledge on a broader set of TOF species. Tree-ring width was identified as the primary method for assessing climate-growth relationships in the studies, while wood anatomy, wood density, and stable isotopes were used less frequently. Our findings indicate a strong positive correlation between precipitation and tree growth across various climates, while temperature exhibited mixed effects. The underrepresentation of studies in the Tropics and the Southern Hemisphere, the taxonomic composition of TOF dendroecology, and the predominance from ring width as a parameter to study growth highlight a critical bias in current knowledge. To advance TOF dendroecology, future research must prioritize sampling sites where TOFs are highly present, obtaining metadata related to management and stand origin, and adopting a multi-parameter approach to understand climate-growth relationships to create a more comprehensive framework for understanding global tree-growth dynamics .

title: Resource depletion
summary: This entry examines resource depletion, its various types, impacts, and mitigation strategies. Resource depletion occurs when natural resources are consumed faster than they can replenish, categorized into renewable and non-renewable resour
content: This entry examines resource depletion, its various types, impacts, and mitigation strategies. Resource depletion occurs when natural resources are consumed faster than they can replenish, categorized into renewable and non-renewable resource depletion. Key environmental impacts include habitat destruction, biodiversity loss, and climate change. Social and economic consequences entail instability, inequality, and geopolitical tensions. It emphasizes sustainable resource management practices such as conservation, circular economy principles, and technological innovations like renewable energy and efficient resource use. It highlights the role of international cooperation through Sustainable Development Goals and regulatory frameworks designed to promote responsible resource consumption. Understanding the complex interdependencies between resources is crucial for holistic management. The document concludes that balancing economic growth with sustainability challenges demands technological advances and behavior shifts, while ongoing research and cooperative efforts are vital for a sustainable future. This review aims to inform strategies addressing the pressing issue of resource depletion.

title: Anàlisi i desenrotllament de nous elements de protecció contra l'abrasió per a esports de carrera i patinatge
summary: [ES] En los últimos años, la popularidad de los deportes sobre ruedas ha aumentado a medida que las personas priorizan su salud y dedican su tiempo libre a la práctica deportiva para llevar un estilo de vida más saludable. Sin embargo, exis
content: [ES] En los últimos años, la popularidad de los deportes sobre ruedas ha aumentado a medida que las personas priorizan su salud y dedican su tiempo libre a la práctica deportiva para llevar un estilo de vida más saludable. Sin embargo, existe una brecha en la mejora de los elementos de protección contra la abrasión utilizados en este tipo de deporte mediante el aprovechamiento de tecnologías modernas como la impresión 3D. Actualmente, las marcas más populares no utilizan esta tecnología en sus productos. No obstante, varios estudios han explorado la viabilidad de utilizar impresoras 3D para fabricar elementos de protección como rodilleras y comprobar sus propiedades mecánicas. Existe una brecha en la evaluación de la comodidad de estas prendas. Se crean varios diseños en función de diversos parámetros como el peso, el tiempo de impresión, la adaptabilidad, la superficie de contacto y la rigidez; se selecciona el mejor diseño para su fabricación. Se utilizó PLA para imprimir los elementos sólidos, y el soporte está hecho de elastano y tejido de polietileno. La resistencia a la abrasión de las prendas se probó con papel de lija adherido a un taladro, y la comodidad de las rodilleras se evaluó con patinadores, ciclistas de BMX, patinadores en línea y participantes voluntarios que realizaron una serie de ejercicios de carrera. Tras probar las prendas, completaron una encuesta. En cuanto a la comodidad, solo los ciclistas de BMX encontraron una diferencia significativa entre las tres rodilleras; el diseño favorito fue el que no utilizaba elementos sólidos. Las respuestas de los demás participantes no mostraron diferencias significativas entre los diseños. Tras la prueba preliminar de lavado, las piezas de las rodilleras no mostraron deterioro, y en cuanto a la protección contra la abrasión, el diseño sin elementos sólidos mostró la mejor resistencia.

title: Dielectric stacking-engineered scalable reconfigurable transistor platform for adaptive logic circuits
summary: Abstract Although reconfigurable van der Waals devices featuring flexible logic transformation offer a promising strategy toward adaptable architectures to accommodate diverse computational demands, reliable polarity control and scalable in
content: Abstract Although reconfigurable van der Waals devices featuring flexible logic transformation offer a promising strategy toward adaptable architectures to accommodate diverse computational demands, reliable polarity control and scalable integration remain challenging. Here, we demonstrate a reconfigurable field-effect transistor based on the scalable dielectric oxide-van der Waals quasi-floating-gate configuration, enabling nonvolatile polarity switching and multi-state programmability. Charge trapping engineering in an atomic-layer Al 2 O 3 /HfO 2 /Al 2 O 3 dielectric stack achieves performance with nonvolatile conductance update (>6-bits for 1000 s), robust endurance (>3 × 10 5 cycles), and well-balanced electron/hole transport (current mismatch ratio ~ 1%). TCAD simulation and surface potential analysis reveal oxygen vacancies-dominated polarity switching dynamics. Using a silicon-compatible top-gate dielectric process and complementary design, diverse logic gates—including eight Boolean operations and seamless AND-OR-Invert/OR-AND-Invert transformations—are accommodated into compact reconfigurable logic-in-memory circuits. These transistors also simplify ternary content-addressable memory design, underscoring their potential for efficient logic-in-memory computing.

title: Integrated in silico and in vitro analysis of oxyphyllacinol in low back pain–associated neuroinflammation
summary: Neuroinflammation and sensitization-related mechanisms may contribute to persistent low back pain (LBP), motivating investigation of compounds that can modulate these processes. This study integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking,
content: Neuroinflammation and sensitization-related mechanisms may contribute to persistent low back pain (LBP), motivating investigation of compounds that can modulate these processes. This study integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, and in vitro experiments to investigate the anti-neuroinflammatory effects of oxyphyllacinol and its potential relevance to LBP-associated pathways. Candidate targets of oxyphyllacinol were predicted using the SwissTargetPrediction, BATMAN-TCM, and SuperPred databases, and the results were intersected with LBP-associated genes obtained from the GeneCards and OMIM databases. Protein–protein interaction network analysis identified PTGS2, TRPV1, CNR1, and COMT as candidate hub targets. Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analyses indicated associations with neuroactive ligand–receptor interaction and with the regulation of TRP channels by inflammatory mediators. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding poses of oxyphyllacinol with the four candidate proteins. Biological validation was performed in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated BV2 microglia. Oxyphyllacinol reduced LPS-stimulated PGE2, TNF-α, and IL-6 release, and decreased PTGS2 and TRPV1 messenger RNA expression, while increasing CNR1 and COMT messenger RNA expression (all p < 0.01). These findings demonstrate the anti-inflammatory activity of oxyphyllacinol in an in vitro microglial model and support further investigation of PTGS2-, TRPV1-, CNR1-, and COMT-associated pathways. Because the experimental validation was limited to an LPS-stimulated cell model, the results should be interpreted as preliminary mechanistic evidence rather than direct evidence of therapeutic efficacy in LBP.
